item.title: Meta now has over 100 different AI glasses styles, and I got to try every new pair, including some that ditch the camera
item.dc:content:
New month, new Ray-Bans. That's certainly what Meta seems to think these days, as it's launching nearly 10 new AI glasses at Meta Connect 2026.

These come hot on the heels of the company's July event that launched a slew of new glasses under the "Meta AI Glasses" brand. September's new reveals include three new Meta AI Glasses-branded glasses, a brand-new Ray-Ban Gen 3 line with three main styles, and another brand-new line called Ray-Ban Audio that ditches the cameras altogether.

That, and Meta announced a new partnership with superstar musician LISA, bringing the artist's style to two Meta AI glasses styles, plus blindbox charms that come with each pair. Here's everything you can expect.

Upgrades for (nearly) all Meta AI glasses

All new Meta AI glasses launch with the features I'm about to detail, but most existing pairs will get them too, starting with customizable controls that let you change the function of the buttons and touchpads to launch apps or run commands.

Meta AI glasses with cameras now support landscape mode cropping, which will automatically crop images taken with your glasses and straighten them using AI. A new dynamic camera feature can also be enabled to take a burst of photos when you press the shutter, letting you select the best photo after capture.

The audio experience is also getting an upgrade with Dolby Atmos-certified playback, so you get proper surround sound when watching videos with your Meta AI glasses connected to your phone. You'll also be able to customize the left/rigth audio balance, or select mono audio for a louder output.

Last is what Meta calls a groundbreaking new FDA-approved mode named Hearing Enhancement, which uses the glasses' microphones to amplify what someone in front of you is saying. That audio is then immediately played back through the glasses' speakers, which reside over your ear, helping replace hearing aids for some people.

I tried this feature using earplugs to simulate hearing loss and was impressed with how much easier it was to hear the Meta rep talk to me. I'd like to see how it works for someone with actual hearing loss, but the demo felt legit. This feature is coming to select Meta AI glasses, which means all the new models plus a handful of older ones, but it's an extra $149 upcharge to enable the feature. Meta One subscribers get the feature included in their plans.

Ray-Ban Meta Audio

I tried the new Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses at the Hearing Enhancement booth, and they're exactly what you'd expect: cameraless Meta AI glasses. Meta says it chose this because people mainly use the audio function on camera glasses, but it's clear the company is also responding to the privacy issues plaguing the brand.

There are no new exclusive features here, just the optional $149 Hearing Enhancement add-on if you need it. Ray-Ban Meta Audio Glasses come in two main styles: Burbank, which looks pretty similar to Wayfarer to me, and Clubmaster, which is a radically different style from the rest of the pack. Clubmaster would be my style pick, for sure.

Since there's no camera, these weigh just 42g and feel substantially lighter because of it. Every gram counts with glasses, and it shows here. These start at $349 and will be available on October 7.

Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3

It's hard to believe Meta is already launching a 3rd-generation Ray-Ban Meta product, but it's here with some surprisingly light upgrades over last year's pair. They launch in the classic Wayfarer style, as well as two new ones: Aviator and Zena.

Aviator is a larger, more structured style with wide lenses, while Zena pulls things in for a more feminine look. The limited-edition Warm Beige Aviators particularly appealed to me, though they'll run you an eye-watering $549. All three models come in black and Havana, plus select "seasonal" options and the usual lens types and colors.

Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 sports one extra mic (for a total of 6) and an additional hour of battery life over Gen 2 models. Gen 3 also has the customizable action button from July's Meta AI Glasses, as well as the slightly upgraded chipset, but, curiously, doesn't feature the adjustable nose pads. Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses retail for $449 and up, and are available right now.

LISA needs glasses

Meta AI glasses may have launched just two months ago, but Meta is already debuting four new options so people can buy another pair. The main new styles are Capri, which looks somewhat similar to the Adventurer style but with a more cat-eye appearance, and Nova, which has nicely rounded frames. Both pairs start at $299.

In addition to that, Meta is partnering with renowned musician LISA and launching special LISA versions of the Adventurer and Capri styles. These colorways, as Meta called them, feature unique color accents and a trademark star on each temple tip.

Each pair comes with a specially styled case, blind-box-style pet charms that clip onto the case, and unique digital photocards in the Meta AI app, all for $399. Meta is also launching a new $249 pair of Meta AI Glasses with a black frame and grey lenses in the Adventurer style, making them the most affordable pair yet.
item.description: Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3, Ray-Ban Meta Audio, and a slew of new Meta AI Glasses styles just made their debut at Meta Connect 2026.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Sutrich
item.dc:description: <p>Nick started with DOS and NES and uses those fond memories of floppy disks and cartridges to fuel his opinions on modern tech. Because of this, he covers both smartphones and VR technology, two avenues that split his passions right down the middle. From Nokia fan to Android fanatic, Nick has been writing about and reviewing smartphones since 2011. An avid gamer and equally well-versed tech head, Nick worked in the IT industry for 15 years, helping to further develop his technical knowledge, which has become particularly important in his fight with PWM sensitivity and deep dives into display technology. He's a huge fan of any phone that can fold in half and loves getting into the nitty-gritty with folding phone coverage for the site. He's also got over a decade of experience with VR gaming, having used the original Oculus DK1 and every major VR headset since then, passionately covering Android Central's Meta Quest content and smart glasses coverage with his weekly thVRsday column on Thursdays. Beyond that, you'll find Nick taking photos of anything and everything, from the beautiful mountains of his home to the chickens in his backyard, and using them to compare cameras to help you choose the best one.</p>

item.title: The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Plus have no secrets left, and they're not cheap
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Samsung is reportedly focusing on the Galaxy Tab S12 Plus and Ultra, thus ditching the base variant.
  • The Plus could get a 12.6-inch 120Hz AMOLED display, while the Ultra keeps its massive 14.6-inch panel.
  • Both tablets are powered by the 3nm Dimensity 9500 chip, with leaked benchmarks pointing to a major performance leap over the previous generation.

Samsung’s upcoming flagship tablets are shaping up to be a fairly conservative upgrade, with the Galaxy Tab S12 Plus and Tab S12 Ultra rumored to be bringing a new MediaTek chip and minor changes to the battery.

The Korean tech giant is not expected to release a standard Galaxy Tab S12, with the company instead focusing on the Plus and Ultra models. The Tab S12 Plus is said to feature a 12.6-inch 120Hz Dynamic AMOLED 2X display with a resolution of 2,800 x 1,752, while the Ultra could stick to its giant 14.6-inch 120Hz panel with a resolution of 2,960 x 1,848, according to WinFuture.

Both phones are said to be powered by MediaTek’s 3nm Dimensity 9500 and come with 12GB of RAM as standard under the hood. The Ultra could pack up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, and both tablets are expected to provide microSD expansion. Samsung seems to be sticking with its aluminum construction, IP68 protection, and bundled S Pen, too.

The Plus may pack a 10,600mAh battery, while the Ultra is said to retain its 11,600mAh cell. The outlet reports that both can charge at 45W. The Plus is also said to tip the scales at 555 grams, making it lighter than Samsung's previous Plus tablet, even with the larger battery.

Another potentially bigger change is happening under the hood: the Dimensity 9500 has already shown up in a Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra Geekbench listing, with reported scores significantly higher than the previous Tab S11 Ultra. That points to performance—rather than a visual redesign—as Samsung’s biggest practical upgrade.

The more important question is price. Previous leaks priced Tab S12 Plus at $1,200 for 256GB and Ultra at $1,400 for 256GB. The European pricing is said to be €1,299 and €1,539, respectively.

Those numbers are still not official, but earlier leaks already pointed to a big bump in price over the Tab S11 generation, especially for the Ultra.

The two tablets are tipped to launch on October 7, and just how much that familiar hardware package actually costs will be determined by Samsung’s final pricing.
item.description: The Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is said to promise massive power, if your wallet can handle it.

item.title: Band together: Qualcomm founds 'Personal AI Health Alliance' with Global Health Connector and more
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Qualcomm and Global Health Connector announce a partnership as the companies found the Personal AI Health Alliance.
  • The PAIHA's purpose is to make the health data our wearables capture mean something with a more proactive, detailed, and accessible mindset.
  • Continuous health data capture, secure information, and more are a major focus.

New chips for our phones are probably what we look forward to the most at Snapdragon Summit. However, Qualcomm's coming forward with a new partnership—or rather, a new alliance for our health.

Over in Belfast, U.K., AI-powered health solutions were the name of the game for Qualcomm and its partner, Global Health Connector. According to a press release, the two companies have joined forces to leverage AI for our health and create the Personal AI Health Alliance (PAIHA). While these two companies are at the helm, Optum Health, Scripps Health, MERCK, Digital Medicine Society, and Biocom, among others, are also involved.

The PAIHA reportedly has "three main beliefs" that are steering its focus moving forward. The first involves remaining "perceptive." Wearables should provide "richer health insights" through continuous, real-world sensing. The post builds on this, stating AI-powered health solutions show promise in delivering crucial information to users and health providers daily.

Staying "proximal" is another aspect of having AI solutions that are a seamless part of our daily lives. Specifically, this concerns the storage and processing of the user's health data. The Personal AI Health Alliance wants user data to remain private by implementing on-device AI to "reduce exposure associated with transmitting data..."

This is an ongoing process, though; one that the alliance states it will continue to work on and research. Finally, there's the "proactive" side of what the Health Alliance is chasing. Delivering "timely" and "relevant" health insights to users is important for the user's well-being. However, the PAIHA also sees this as a way to "reduce costs or validate drug efficacy."

Rich data should mean something

We're still at the beginning of the PAIHA, but it states that it has provided proof of concept and more. Echoing its beliefs, the PAIHA states these AI-powered solutions aim to make health data "more continuous." However, your health data is yours. It should feel personal, while also remaining accessible. Bleddyn Rees, Global Health Connector, said, "Healthcare is data-rich but often insight-poor. The real opportunity lies in turning data into actionable intelligence that improves outcomes for everyone."

We've seen similar sentiments and an urge to make continuous health recording mean something before. This seems to be the direction this space is headed. With a stronger alliance such as the PAIHA, perhaps the future looks bright.
item.description: Qualcomm, Global Health Connect found the "Personal AI Health Alliance" for wearable AI solutions that make all of our health data mean something.

item.title: Qualcomm's premium audio leaps ahead with Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 and its personal AI
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Qualcomm revealed the Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2, its latest advancement in its premium audio technology.
  • The chip offers "industry-leading" audio tech with adaptive ANC and aptX Lossless support, with "context-aware" listening.
  • The Sound Elite Gen 2's personal AI will assist users daily with requests and tasks given, while keeping its power consumption low and your audio experience strong.

It feels like it's been a while since Qualcomm's premium audio technology. That's precisely why, at Snapdragon Summit, the company announced the next generation of Snapdragon Sound.

This afternoon, Qualcomm revealed the Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2. Its press release positions the Sound Elite Gen 2 as a "premium audio platform purpose-built for personal AI..." Qualcomm states that it combined on-device AI, cloud-connected capabilities, and "industry-leading" audio tech for this new chip. However, it's the audio power of the Sound Elite Gen 2 that's the main focus.

Qualcomm says it's reworked the new chip to feature immersive, "high-fidelity" audio for wireless devices. Consumers should notice these improvements while listening to music, voices, shows/movies, games, and more. The chip's aptX Lossless support delivers "bit-for-bit" music streaming, meaning you won't miss a beat and every sound is delivered with clarity.

Qualcomm is reportedly confident that this higher-quality sound will remain consistent over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. On the other hand, you have Qualcomm's AI that can reportedly "continuously respond to the user." The AI will account for your activity and your environment while you're listening to ensure everything remains clear. Adaptive ANC (active noise cancellation) and "context-aware listening" are two major hallmarks. The chip's AI is also fully capable of taking user requests.

In short, it can assist with translations, retrieving information, and more.

Qualcomm Sound

With everything new and improved Qualcomm's worked on, there's a concern about the toll on our phones. The company states the Snapdragon Sound Elite Gen 2 features "up to 40% lower power consumption" compared to previous generations. What's more, Qualcomm sees the chip headed to "intelligent hearables." Such devices include premium AI earbuds, open-ear devices, audio glasses, camera buds, hearing and wellness devices, and AI wearables.

Other areas include qobuz, cinemo, and more. Much of the Sound Elite Gen 2's AI assistance is enhanced by its Wi-Fi 6E support. Qualcomm says this offers direct-to-cloud connectivity that "makes always-on personal AI" possible. The post states this is more "practical," as to not compromise your battery life and audio listening experience.
item.description: Qualcomm's Snapdragon Sound advances with the Elite Gen 2, sporting adaptive ANC, personal AI, "context-aware" audio, and much more.

item.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro series stuns with privacy screen and wondrous rear displays—debuts 'Special Edition,' too
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Xiaomi launched the 18 Pro series in China this week, stating the 18 Pro Max features a 6.9-inch main display and a 2.9-inch rear display.
  • The Xiaomi 18 Pro features a 6.4-inch screen and a 2.7-inch rear display; however, both phones feature the new privacy screen with "location-based triggers."
  • This privacy screen will automatically hide content on your phone depending on your location, which may carry sensitive information (alerts, floating windows, etc.).
  • The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at 6,999 CNY (~$1,042), while the 18 Pro begins at 5,999 CNY (~$900).

The wait is over; Xiaomi's 18 Pro series is here. The Chinese OEM has launched its latest flagship phones for its consumers, and there's new tech and new features to explore.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro and Pro Max debuted in China early this morning (via GSMArena). Getting us started is the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max with Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. The device features a 6.9-inch AMOLED front display and a 2.9-inch rear screen. For the moment, we'll focus on the main display, since Xiaomi has equipped it with a proactive privacy screen.

This will sound similar to what Samsung did with the Galaxy S26 Ultra; however, the publication notes one major difference: Xiaomi uses "location-based triggers." This privacy screen will activate depending on where you are to block anything carrying sensitive information (notifications, floating windows, etc.). The rear display now benefits from Xiaomi's AI, Xiao, for mini-app creation, timers, and reminders.

There are three cameras on the 18 Pro Max: a 200MP main lens, a 200MP periscope telephoto sensor, and a 50MP ultrawide camera. The selfie camera reportedly arrives at 50MP. Powering the phone is an 8,500mAh battery with 100W wired and 50W wireless charging capabilities. Xiaomi officially lists the 18 Pro Max with five RAM/storage configurations. Consumers will find an entry 12/256GB up to a 16/1TB option.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at 6,999 CNY (~$1,042). The phone is available in China in black, white, blue, and pink; however, there is a Special Edition transparent red option (16/1TB). A global launch is expected, something that Xiaomi mentioned during the Snapdragon Summit. Details about it will likely come at a later date

Xiaomi 18 Pro

There are a few similarities between the 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max, but we'll begin with what separates them. The Xiaomi 18 Pro features a slightly smaller 6.4-inch AMOLED main screen and a 2.7-inch rear display. The OEM opted for Qualcomm's "more efficient" Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 for the 18 Pro and a 7,000mAh battery with similar charging capabilities.

For what remains continuous, the 18 Pro features the same triple camera array as the 18 Pro Max: a 200MP main lens, a 200MP periscope telephoto sensor, and a 50MP ultrawide camera. Additionally, Xiaomi placed its new privacy screen with location-based triggers on the 18 Pro, too. Other tools, such as Xiao AI and the mini-app creation for the rear display, remain on the 18 Pro.

Xiaomi lists the 18 Pro with the same color assortment as the 18 Pro, including the red transparent Special Edition. The phone starts at 5,999 CNY (~$900). Consumers in China will find it in four RAM/storage configurations: 12/256GB, 12/512GB, 16/512GB, 16/1TB.

Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit is going on. Yesterday (Sept. 22), Xiaomi's SVP and president of international business, Adam Zeng, took the stage to tease the 18 Pro series. Adam Zeng said that the Xiaomi 18 Pro series will be the first phones to feature Qualcomm's Dual 8 Elites: the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Each chip is designed for a different purpose. While both are strong, Qualcomm says the 8 Elite Gen 6 is "built for efficiency," while the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 is more focused on "peak performance."

What you need to know

  • Xiaomi launched the 18 Pro series in China this week, stating the 18 Pro Max features a 6.9-inch main display and a 2.9-inch rear display.
  • The Xiaomi 18 Pro features a 6.4-inch screen and a 2.7-inch rear display; however, both phones feature the new privacy screen with "location-based triggers."
  • This privacy screen will automatically hide content on your phone depending on your location, which may carry sensitive information (alerts, floating windows, etc.).
  • The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at 6,999 CNY (~$1,042), while the 18 Pro begins at 5,999 CNY (~$900).

The wait is over; Xiaomi's 18 Pro series is here. The Chinese OEM has launched its latest flagship phones for its consumers, and there's new tech and new features to explore.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro and Pro Max debuted in China early this morning (via GSMArena). Getting us started is the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max with Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. The device features a 6.9-inch AMOLED front display and a 2.9-inch rear screen. For the moment, we'll focus on the main display, since Xiaomi has equipped it with a proactive privacy screen.

This will sound similar to what Samsung did with the Galaxy S26 Ultra; however, the publication notes one major difference: Xiaomi uses "location-based triggers." This privacy screen will activate depending on where you are to block anything carrying sensitive information (notifications, floating windows, etc.). The rear display now benefits from Xiaomi's AI, Xiao, for mini-app creation, timers, and reminders.

There are three cameras on the 18 Pro Max: a 200MP main lens, a 200MP periscope telephoto sensor, and a 50MP ultrawide camera. The selfie camera reportedly arrives at 50MP. Powering the phone is an 8,500mAh battery with 100W wired and 50W wireless charging capabilities. Xiaomi officially lists the 18 Pro Max with five RAM/storage configurations. Consumers will find an entry 12/256GB up to a 16/1TB option.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max starts at 6,999 CNY (~$1,042). The phone is available in China in black, white, blue, and pink; however, there is a Special Edition transparent red option (16/1TB). A global launch is expected, something that Xiaomi mentioned during the Snapdragon Summit. Details about it will likely come at a later date

Xiaomi 18 Pro

There are a few similarities between the 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max, but we'll begin with what separates them. The Xiaomi 18 Pro features a slightly smaller 6.4-inch AMOLED main screen and a 2.7-inch rear display. The OEM opted for Qualcomm's "more efficient" Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 for the 18 Pro and a 7,000mAh battery with similar charging capabilities.

For what remains continuous, the 18 Pro features the same triple camera array as the 18 Pro Max: a 200MP main lens, a 200MP periscope telephoto sensor, and a 50MP ultrawide camera. Additionally, Xiaomi placed its new privacy screen with location-based triggers on the 18 Pro, too. Other tools, such as Xiao AI and the mini-app creation for the rear display, remain on the 18 Pro.

Xiaomi lists the 18 Pro with the same color assortment as the 18 Pro, including the red transparent Special Edition. The phone starts at 5,999 CNY (~$900). Consumers in China will find it in four RAM/storage configurations: 12/256GB, 12/512GB, 16/512GB, 16/1TB.

Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit is going on. Yesterday (Sept. 22), Xiaomi's SVP and president of international business, Adam Zeng, took the stage to tease the 18 Pro series. Adam Zeng said that the Xiaomi 18 Pro series will be the first phones to feature Qualcomm's Dual 8 Elites: the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Each chip is designed for a different purpose. While both are strong, Qualcomm says the 8 Elite Gen 6 is "built for efficiency," while the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 is more focused on "peak performance."

item.title: Forget the Pixel 10a - this is the best Android phone under $500, and it just scored a rare discount at Amazon
item.dc:content:
Tech keeps getting more and more expensive, but that doesn't mean that you can't find the occasional cheap Android phone deal if you know where to look. Grab the unlocked Nothing Phone (4a) Pro from Amazon today, for example, and you'll get a straight $50 off your purchase. That knocks the price of the midrange masterpiece down to just $449!

The Nothing Phone (4a) Pro easily holds its own against midrange Android phones like the Google Pixel 10a and the Samsung Galaxy A57 5G, blending eye-catching design and a 144Hz AMOLED display with efficient Snapdragon performance and a large 5,080mAh battery.

This deal comes just a few weeks before Amazon's Big Deal Days sale on October 6th and 7th, but why wait for Prime Day when you can score a discount on a great cheap Android phone today? After all, it's unlikely that the price will dip much further when the sale begins in earnest, and you run the risk of stock selling out if you wait too long.

  • Prime Big Deal Days returns October 6-7: see the full list of early deals

Nothing Phone (4a) Pro 128GB: $499 $449 at Amazon

Grab the 128GB Nothing Phone (4a) Pro unlocked from Amazon today and you'll score a straight $50 off your purchase, no strings attached. You can also upgrade to the 256GB configuration of the phone and increase your discount to $90 off.

No trade-in is required, although Amazon is offering up to $500 in the form of a gift card when you send in an old or broken device as part of your order. View Deal

Reviewer Nick Sutrich called the Nothing Phone (4a) Pro the 'only $499 phone I'd buy' in his 4.5/5-star review earlier this year, and looking at the specs, it isn't hard to see why. The cheap Android phone boasts incredible build quality with one of the best-looking designs in the business, plus you get a gorgeous 144Hz AMOLED display with PWM dimming, plenty of on-device AI features, and six years of software support guaranteed.

The 128GB configuration of the phone also comes with 8GB of RAM, while the 256GB version will increase that to 12GB. Constructed from a metal unibody with an IP65 resistance rating, the Phone (4a) Pro also features a large 5,080mAh battery that will easily last over a day on a single charge, while unique features like Essential Space and Nothing Playground ensure that you're getting a flagship-quality software experience without paying a flagship price.

As far as hardware is concerned, the Phone (4a) Pro utilizes a Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 chipset that falls a bit behind the Google Pixel 10a's Tensor G4 when looking at peak performance, but it's crucial to note that the Snapdragon CPU performs more efficiently over longer periods of time. The Pixel 10a, on the other hand, is known to overheat, making it less reliable for regular daily use.

Each phone has their own strengths and weaknesses, but if I was trying to decide between the Pixel 10a and the Nothing Phone (4a) Pro, I'd choose the device that takes risks over the same-old, same-old.
item.description: Amazon just dropped a rare discount on the Nothing Phone (4a) Pro, one of the most unique midrange phones on the market.

Whether you’re a veteran tech-head or a novice, Patrick offers honest, no-nonsense shopping advice with years of hands-on experience to back it up. item.title: Motorola preps a huge Qira AI expansion to Signature, Razr with Android 17
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Motorola and Lenovo's always-on AI, Qira, receives a major phone expansion with the company's Android 17 upgrade.
  • Qira is a context-aware AI that helps users find new outfits with "Style Sync" or stay in the loop with "Catch me up."
  • Motorola says that with its Android 17 upgrade, consumers should look out for Qira on the Signature, Razr, and Edge series.

Motorola and Lenovo's system-level intelligence, Qira, is expanding to more phones this week with Android 17. Motorola details which devices will see Qira in this new expansion.

At the start of Qualcomm's Snapdragon Summit, Motorola got a Qira announcement out of the way regarding its Android 17 upgrade. If Qira is supported, Moto says users can take the AI's assistance with them from their phone, desktop, watch, and PC. With the "Hey Qira" wake word, Moto says the AI can provide "features like Catch me up, the ability to ask urgent questions, and a knowledge base that features all of their saved files, preferences, and synced cross-device information."

Permitting Qira activates another level of assistance for your Motorola phone. Continuing a project from your phone on your PC is one of those unlocked features. What's more, "Pay Attention" helps users with transcribed audio recordings that "summarize key points." You can also find "Next Move." This feature suggests what you should do next. If you're reading a blog post, it might ask if you want a summary. Or if you've booked a flight, Qira might suggest setting a reminder so you're on time.

"Catch me up" keeps you in the loop with a round-up of notifications, news, and more, while "Style Sync" brings Qira in for new fashion styles. A collaboration with Lenovo's Workato lets users lean on Qira to complete tasks for them (if told to) and quickly find important information in their email.

Android 17 is where Moto users can expect to find Qira's massive expansion. Motorola is being selective, stating you'll see Qira on its Signature, Razr, and Edge devices.

Moto AI

We were introduced to Qira earlier this year. The AI was a pretty big swing from Motorola and Lenovo, as the two companies went beyond "simple chatbots" to a "personal ambient intelligence" system. The point of Qira is to create an experience that's always-on and consistent across Android, PC, and more. In conjunction with "Next Move" and "Catch me up," users can chat with Qira.

Additionally, Motorola says you can chat via voice, text, images, or videos. Qira is wrapped inside the Moto AI feature suite. Remaining context-aware is key for Motorola and Lenovo. It's one significant way for the AI to deliver the assistance it was designed to do. Of course, much of this is based on its level of permissions. If users don't want it inside their emails or notifications for "Catch me up," you don't have to let it.
item.description: Qira AI is on the way to a few of Motorola's best phones with its Android 17 upgrade for always-on assistance.

item.title: Concerned about your eye health? You can get the innovative TCL 50 XL NXTPAPER 5G for free with this Total Wireless deal — here’s how
item.dc:content:
Let's face it: we spend a lot of time staring at screens, so it's no wonder that many folks are searching for devices that utilize eye-friendly display technology. TCL is a leading manufacturer in this regard, and you can get one of their best phones for FREE by adding a line with an eligible data plan at Total Wireless.

The last-gen TCL 50 XL NXTPAPER 5G boasts a 6.78-inch eye-friendly display with a 120Hz refresh rate and multiple display modes, making it ideal for users with PWM sensitivity. The matte, paper-like finish of the screen is perfect for reducing glare and eye strain, while the RGB sensor automatically adjusts the color temperature depending on the time of day. The TCL 50 XL also comes with an SD slot for expandable storage, 8GB of RAM, and a 5,100mAh battery, all of which are rare specs for a phone in this price range.

TCL 50 XL NXTPAPER 5G 128GB: $99.99 FREE with Total Max 5G plan or higher at Total Wireless

Join Total Wireless with a new line on the Total Max 5G plan (or higher) and the Verizon-owned carrier will hook you up with a free TCL 50 XL NXTPAPER 5G, no trade-in required. Even if you go with a more-affordable data plan, Total will still give you the eye-friendly smartphone for just $19.99 with ANY new line activation. View Deal

The Total Max 5G plan starts at $50 per month for a single line with AutoPay, although the price drops a lot when you add multiple lines. The plan gives you unlimited talk, text, and 5G Ultra Wideband data on Verizon's vast network, plus you get an unlimited mobile hotspot and free calling to and from Mexico included in the package.

Your plan also comes with a 5-year price guarantee and no confusing contracts or hidden fees to worry about. As an MVNO carrier, what you see is what you get, even if Total Wireless doesn't have as many perks as some premium unlimited plans.

TCL proves that the latest innovations in display technology don't have to cost an arm and a leg, and now that they've partnered up with Total Wireless, protecting your long-term vision health is easier (and more affordable) than ever before.

item.title: Amazfit just pulled off the solar AMOLED trick Garmin couldn't
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Amazfit has unveiled the T-Rex Dual Solar, its first dual-sided solar AMOLED smartwatch that collects sunlight from both the front and rear.
  • A larger panel sits inside the glass-ceramic rear plate, which Amazfit claims has twice the collection area, so the watch keeps charging even when it's off your wrist.
  • Its 660mAh battery is said to deliver 25 days of standard use (or 41 hours in Accuracy GPS mode), extending up to 34 days with three daily hours of direct sunlight.

If you’re in the market for a rugged outdoor watch with great battery life that’s built to withstand off-grid excursions, Garmin’s Fenix series has long held a monopoly on your wrist. But it makes you choose between a battery-sipping, washed-out Memory-in-Pixel (MIP) display with solar, or a rich, vibrant AMOLED display, and settle for shorter battery life. Amazfit's new T-Rex Dual Solar takes a different approach: keep the bright AMOLED display and add solar charging to both sides of the watch.

The T-Rex Dual Solar is the brand's first-ever AMOLED smartwatch with dual-sided solar charging. The front display can harness sunlight while you’re wearing it, and a larger solar panel is inside the glass-ceramic rear plate. Amazfit says the rear panel has twice the collection area of the front one, giving you another option when the watch is not on your wrist.

That means a somewhat surreal but actually useful backup plan: if the battery dies, you can flip the watch over and expose its back to the sun, or just leave it in a sunny place, to get enough power to boot essential functions back up. The watch also has a Solar Priority Mode to help you get the most out of this off-wrist charging.

Amazfit rates the 660mAh battery for up to 25 days of typical use and 41 hours in Accuracy GPS mode. Under the test conditions described, 50,000 lux for three hours a day can extend typical battery life up to 34 days.

The rest of the package is suitably rugged too, with a 1.32-inch AMOLED display with a peak brightness of 3,000 nits, sapphire crystal, a Grade 5 titanium bezel, 10 ATM water resistance, maps, turn-by-turn navigation, waypoint tools, ski maps, and LiveShare location tracking. Plus, there's a red-light flashlight for night use.

The catch is the cost. Amazfit is stepping up into the premium adventure watch arena with this $650 offering, rather than its usual value-focused space. The T-Rex Dual Solar is now available on Amazfit's website and Amazon, and real-world testing will determine if its dual-sided solar system can live up to its lofty battery promises.
item.description: Amazfit's new $650 adventure watch has a solar panel on its back, and it can revive a dead battery.

item.title: Mint Mobile’s best deal ends next week — claim up to a year of unlimited wireless for $15 per month (while you still can)
item.dc:content:
If you're sick of paying an arm and a leg for wireless, there's a Mint Mobile deal that you should be checking out immediately. For a limited time, the T-Mobile-owned carrier is dropping all of its data plans down to just $15 per month, regardless of the plan length or data allotment. And yes, that includes Mint's popular unlimited tier.

This Mint Mobile deal has been available for a while, but the carrier is planning to officially retire the promotion on September 30th. That means you have less than a week to sign up before the wireless plans return to their original price.

The only catch is that, due to Mint's buy-in-bulk plan system, you will have to pay for a minimum of three months to enjoy the savings. item.title: Google thinks the iPhone Duo could actually be good news for Android foldables
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Google believes Apple's entry with the iPhone Duo validates a foldable category Android brands have built for years.
  • The company believes the iPhone Duo's halo effect could increase consumer interest in Android foldable phones as well.
  • A bigger foldable market could finally push developers to properly optimize more apps for Android's larger displays.

Apple is finally entering the foldable smartphone market with the iPhone Duo very soon. And Google actually thinks Apple's arrival in the category could be a good thing.

We've been waiting for a foldable iPhone for years, but it's finally no longer a dream. Apple is opening pre-orders for the iPhone Duo next month, and as expected, the company's entrance into the category is expected to shake things up. Counterpoint even believes Apple could capture around 25% of the foldable smartphone market within a year of the iPhone Duo's launch.

So technically, Google and its Android partners should be worried about Apple jumping into the foldable phones market, right? Apparently not. In fact, Google believes Apple's arrival could be beneficial for the entire category.

Android president Sameer Samat sat down with Tom's Guide this week to talk about the foldable market and the iPhone Duo. Samat, who says he personally uses the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, praised the multitasking experience and noted that Android is often where consumers get to experience new technologies first, with foldables being one example.

But rather than seeing the iPhone Duo as a threat, Google views Apple's entrance as a long-awaited validation of the foldable category that Android manufacturers have been building for years.

Despite the momentum Apple currently has, Samat believes the halo effect of the iPhone Duo could actually increase consumer interest in Android foldables as well. More importantly, he believes a larger foldable market will finally give developers more reason to properly optimize their apps for bigger folding displays.

That's one area where Apple already appears to have an advantage. The company showcased apps like Netflix and Slack properly optimized for the iPhone Duo, while some of those same apps on Android foldables still look like stretched-out versions of their regular phone interfaces.

Samat, however, believes Apple's entrance could help change that. As foldables become more popular across both platforms, developers have more incentive to invest in the form factor, and Google says developers are already in conversations or actively working on better foldable-optimized Android apps.
item.description: Google thinks the iPhone Duo is good for Android.

item.title: I test headphones for a living, and the Beats 360 are a fun and stylish alternative to the AirPods Max 2 that I can't recommend more
item.dc:content:
The Beats 360 are an interesting mix of hardware and design choices, representing a new approach to Beats headphone design. One that has Apple’s fingerprints all over it. They include some great longevity features right out of the box, so let's get into them.

Beats 360 to the Max!

Though Apple acquired Beats in 2014, the company kept its design aesthetic, with seemingly minor visual changes over the years. Twelve years later, Apple has entered the design chat. Beats has been dabbling in expanding color options for Apple accessories, and that “dabbling” shows up in the 360 ecosystem of frames and accessories.

I can’t help but notice the similarities to the AirPods Max 2. With their thin, round, telescoping arms and flatter cups, the new headphones look like they belong in a Max product lineup, rather than alongside Beats’ current headphone offerings.

This year, Beats introduces four frame colors, along with six performance knit and two ultra plush cushion color kits. Each kit includes ear cushions and a headband and costs $50. Beats says that gives you up to 256 combinations if you mix ear and headband cushions.

I have the Sky frames for review, and like the other three frame color options, these come with color-matched Performance Knit Sky ear cushions and headband. Beats also sent me a Volt Performance Knit kit (pictured on the headphones) and a Cloud UltraPlush kit.

The headbands are extremely simple to swap out. I just pulled the Sky headband off and pushed the Volt headband in. They have knit covers and silicone backs with silicone connectors that have bulbous ends that snap into the frames. The ear cushions also have silicone backs with plastic twist-to-lock nodes that lock into L-shaped grooves in the frames.

Since you get two different cushion densities, which can affect sound, the ear cushions have sensors that tell the frames to adjust the tuning so the sound profile stays consistent. Beats 360 also has a chime that sounds off when the ear cushions are properly seated. The LED on the power button will also turn red if they aren’t seated properly.

During my listening sessions, I didn't hear any distracting differences in tone or timbre between the two cushion styles.

Living to the Beat

The Beats 360 are aimed at active consumers on the go. Over the last week, I've worn them for casual listening and gym sessions. The Performance Knit has done a great job wicking sweat while keeping my ears cooler than most competing ear cushions.

For me and my giant bald head, the knit headband and cushion texture provide enough friction that the 360 stays in place when I lay flat on a bench or lean forward for pushups or barbell rows. The clamping force also makes this possible without becoming fatiguing during extended wear, thanks to the softness of the cushions. When things got really sweaty, the physical controls remained responsive, and for the first time, Beats headphones have an IPX4 protection, so I'm not second-guessing using them for sweaty gym sessions.

When the cushions and headbands get icky, you can hand-wash them with diluted liquid laundry detergent, then air-dry them (avoid the dryer). The only issue users on the go may have is that the headphones no longer fold into a small-ish "ball"; instead, the ear cups rotate flat like the AirPods Max 2, taking up more space in your workout or messenger bag.

Both sets of new ear cushions are much deeper, wider, and more comfortable than the Studio Pros. The only downside to the magnificent ear cups is that they don’t include wear-detection sensors, so they won't automatically play or pause music when you put them on or take them off. A disappointing omission for $350 headphones.

What isn't disappointing is the improved longevity, so you can actually get your money's worth. Beats is offering a $79 mail-in or carry-in battery replacement service similar to the Beats Studio Pro and Solo 4. Beats also says it'll offer a user-replaceable, self-service option in the coming months.

The nine-microphone configuration and noise-cancellation algorithms that give the 360 better ANC than the Beats Studio Pro are a boon for fitness-minded folks. In the gym or on the streets, you'll get noticeably better ANC in the high mids and high frequencies.

While that ANC still doesn’t compete with Bose or Sony for canceling voices and high-frequency noise, it does an admirable job with weight plates clanking about and high-frequency airplane cabin hum.

Beats has actively improved its sound signature since the Solo 3, and the 360s are no exception. We’ve said this over and over, but the muddy sound that pre-Apple Beats headphones had is gone, replaced by a more balanced sound with more prominent mids, greater clarity, and highs that can be a bit stilted on some tracks, teetering on the edge of sibilance.

Despite the lack of Hi-Res Wireless Audio support and the loss of USB-C lossless or 3.5mm wired audio support, you’ll still get respectable detail retrieval when listening to songs like Charles Mingus’ “Moanin’.” Though the instrumentation on “Moanin’” wasn’t the strongest I’ve heard, owing to the lack of higher-bitrate stream support, the ability to pick out different instruments in the arrangement during the most frenetic moments is respectable. I can’t say the same for many Bluetooth headphones, including the venerable Sony WH-1000XM6.

That said, the bass still rumbles on my test tracks from The Roots and Skrillex, but it's tight. The soundstage is large and open, and Dolby Atmos tracks sound fully engaging on the Beats 360.

If you’re an iPhone user, Spatial Audio with movies and content that supports it is very immersive, and I actually prefer listening to music with Spatial Audio activated.

My 360 view of the Beats 360

I called the Powerbeats Fit my favorite workout earbuds, and now I can call Beats 360 my favorite over-ear workout headphones. Just like I do with my smartwatch bands, using a separate pair for working out, daily wear, and sleeping, the ability to switch out a sweaty headband and pair of ear cushions for a dry pair is a delight. The clamping force during workouts is great. The fit and comfort of the UltraPlush cushions for more recreational active listening is wonderful.

If you’re an audiophile or a frequent traveler who prioritizes space-saving carry, you may want to consider competing products along with the Beats 360. If you’re an athlete or someone who hits the gym, the trails, or the urban jungle regularly, this is my Editor’s Choice for you.
item.description: The new Beats 360 looks like the king of active-lifestyle over-ear headphones, with a new design that has Apple's fingerprints all over it.

item.title: Stuffcool made a Qi 2.2 power bank that charges your Apple Watch
item.dc:content:
If you're looking to buy a charger in India, you can't go wrong with Stuffcool. The brand regularly churns out reliable products, and with the Omni Pro, it's making its debut with Qi 2.2 charging tech. The Omni Pro is now available for ₹4,999, and that is in line with other Qi 2.2 power banks I used from the likes of Baseus, Anker, and other global brands.

But the Omni Pro isn't just a standard Qi 2.2 power bank. It also has a swivel arm that swings out, and you can easily charge your Apple Watch on it. This is a brilliant idea, and you don't have to take any other devices if you're heading out with an iPhone and Apple Watch. Oh, and there's also a kickstand, giving you the freedom to plonk your phone on the Omni Pro and use it while charging.

The design is elegant too; Stuffcool went with a silver finish that looks good, and build quality is great — I didn't see any issues in the month I used the power bank. It isn't much bigger than other 10,000mAh power banks, and at 214g, you can slot it into a bag without any issues. There's a tiny panel on the left that shows battery level, and while you don't get charging metrics like the Nexode Pro, it is an easy way of seeing how much charge is left on the power bank.

Qi 2.2 charging tech is interesting because it delivers 25W, and I use it constantly with my iPhone 17 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL. I'm switching to the iPhone 18 Pro Max this week, and it's great to be able to reliably charge these devices without having to connect a cable. The versatility of being able to do so with the Apple Watch is just the icing on the cake.

There's a USB-C cable as well that goes up to 35W, so if you need a faster charge, this is the way to go. The internal battery also charges at 35W, and you get a USB-C cable bundled in the box.

The Omni Pro has a 10,000mAh battery, and it can easily charge the Pixel 11 Pro XL or iPhone 18 Pro Max once over. Standard energy conversion means you don't actually get up to 10,000mAh of usable power — it's around 5,500mAh or so. This is the case with all power banks, and the Omni Pro did a good job delivering consistent power in the month I used it.

There aren't many reliable Qi 2.2 power banks in India, and the Omni Pro is one of the best available in the country. It looks good, does a good job charging devices over the Qi 2.2 standard, and is easy to take anywhere.
item.description: The Omni Pro charges at 25W over Qi 2.2, and it has a dedicated module for your Apple Watch.
item.author: harish.jonnalagadda@futurenet.com (Harish Jonnalagadda)

item.dc:description: <p>Harish Jonnalagadda is Android Central's Senior Editor overseeing the mobile category. He started his tech journey at a very young age by tweaking Windows XP installations, and that hobby ignited an enthusiasm that led him into the world of PC modding. After picking up a Bachelor's degree in computer science, he decided to pursue his passion by covering PC hardware at VR-Zone, where he reviewed motherboards, video cards, and DRAM modules.</p><p><br>While he used iPhones initially, switching to the Nexus 4 served as the catalyst to explore Android's burgeoning ecosystem, and he pivoted to writing about mobile tech, joining Android Central's newsroom back in 2014. As a Senior Editor, he oversees the site's coverage of Chinese phone brands, enthusiast audio products, networking hardware, and storage servers, leveraging his engineering background and extensive experience testing mobile hardware to evaluate the latest phones and accessories.<br></p><p>In over a decade of covering Android, he has used pretty much every single major phone released globally, giving him an unrivaled view into Google's mobile platform. His specialty is Chinese brands; he's charted the growth of all the major Chinese manufacturers from their inception, and he uses that knowledge to share unique insights. When not testing the latest gadgets, he can be found reading sci-fi novels on his e-reader, and occasionally yelling at the TV in frustration as Arsenal squander yet another title run.</p>

item.title: The Galaxy S26 Ultra is finally getting One UI 9 in the US, but there's a catch
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • One UI 9 has started rolling out to some T-Mobile Galaxy S26 Ultra owners in the U.S.
  • The Android 17-based update is around 4GB in size and also includes the September security patch.
  • Unlocked Galaxy S26 phones and models on AT&T and Verizon don't appear to have received the update yet..

Samsung has started rolling out the One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 Ultra owners in the U.S., although it appears to be limited to T-Mobile models for now.

Earlier this month, Samsung announced that One UI 9, which debuted with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series, would begin rolling out to the Galaxy S26 lineup this month. Reports initially suggested the rollout would begin around September 21, but that didn't happen. We later even heard rumors that Samsung may have delayed the Galaxy S26 series' One UI 9 rollout indefinitely.

It now looks like things have taken a U-turn, and there's finally some good news for Samsung users in the U.S. The company appears to have started rolling out One UI 9 to at least some Galaxy S26 Ultra owners.

A user on Reddit reports that their T-Mobile Galaxy S26 Ultra has received the One UI 9 update. As expected, the update is based on Android 17 and comes in at around 4GB. It carries the build number S948USQU4BZID/S948UOYN4BZID/S948USQU4BZID and also includes the September security patch.

A few other users in the Reddit thread have also confirmed receiving the update on their T-Mobile Galaxy S26 Ultra. However, it appears that other Galaxy S26 models on T-Mobile, alongside unlocked devices and phones on AT&T and Verizon, haven't received the update just yet. So, it looks like T-Mobile may have jumped the gun and started rolling out One UI 9 ahead of the wider U.S. release.

That said, if you have a T-Mobile Galaxy S26 Ultra, it's worth heading into Settings and manually checking for the One UI 9 update if you haven't received a notification yet.

There's currently no word on exactly when One UI 9 will arrive for unlocked devices or other carrier variants. But with the update now appearing on T-Mobile models in the U.S., the wait hopefully shouldn't be much longer.

item.title: Garmin just gave some of its best smartwatches a big free upgrade
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Garmin is rolling out a new software update to select Fenix, Forerunner, Venu and Vivoactive smartwatches.
  • The Venu 6 is getting fall detection, which can automatically share your live location with emergency contacts.
  • Select Garmin watches are also gaining hands-free "OK Garmin" voice controls and personalized run workouts.

Garmin has released a new software update for some of its smartwatches, bringing a variety of new features to the ecosystem.

Garmin makes some of the best smartwatches for fitness tracking, and the company continues to improve its devices with regular software updates. Now, Garmin has announced its latest round of features for select watches, including the Fenix 8 series, Forerunner 570, Forerunner 970, Venu 6, and Vivoactive 6.

Garmin says the new features are designed to help users get even more from their devices and take their training to the next level.

With the fall update, Garmin is bringing fall detection to the Venu 6. The feature can send the user's live location to emergency contacts after detecting a hard fall. It's something we've already seen on plenty of Apple and Wear OS smartwatches, but thankfully, Garmin is adding it as well.

Several Garmin smartwatches are also getting hands-free voice controls with a new "OK Garmin" command, allowing users to access certain features without touching their watch.

Garmin is also improving its running features. The update brings personalized run workouts alongside a new adaptive Garmin Run Coach plan, which can adjust training based on the user's performance and progress.

Garmin says the software updates have already started rolling out to compatible devices. Users can check for the latest software through the Garmin Connect app on their phone. If you don't see the update or new features just yet, it's worth checking again over the next few days as the rollout continues.

In addition to its smartwatch updates, Garmin has released new features for its Edge cycling computers as well, including automatic climb and descent detection and switching. Those updates can also be installed through the Garmin Connect app.

We haven't tested the new software on our Garmin smartwatches just yet, but I'm particularly looking forward to trying the new personalized running features. Garmin already excels when it comes to run and training guidance, and these additions could make that part of the experience even better.
item.description: Garmin watches were already great for runners, and this update makes them even better.

item.title: Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 is coming for the top Android phones
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Qualcomm is splitting its top-tier lineup into the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6.
  • Both 2nm platforms center around custom Oryon CPUs, redesigned Adreno GPUs, and Hexagon NPUs tuned to run responsive, context-aware AI assistants locally.
  • APV support and Intelligent Pixel Control aim to deliver better scene understanding and more natural photos and videos.

Qualcomm is doubling down on AI-powered smartphones with two new flagship mobile platforms: the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6. The company says both chips are designed to push on-device AI further while improving gaming, cameras, and connectivity across premium Android phones.

The new Qualcomm lineup is capped out with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. It’s built for high-end Android phones and is very much centered around what Qualcomm calls “everyday agents” — AI that can respond faster, customize experiences, and learn about users during the day.

There are already a handful of likely homes for the Extreme chip. Rumors suggest Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra, while the iQOO 16 has also been associated with the processor in benchmark leaks. Motorola’s upcoming Signature 27 is also said to be in queue for the chipset, but none of these rumors is confirmed.

Qualcomm’s new Adreno Neural Fusion technology uses AI to improve graphics for gamers, and the company says it will lead to better visuals and longer gaming sessions.

The chip also adds new camera features like support for Advanced Professional Video (APV) and Intelligent Pixel Control, which is designed to help the camera understand the scene better and deliver more natural-looking photos and video.

Meanwhile, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 is a bit more broad in its approach. It’s based on the same 2nm process and packs Qualcomm’s custom Oryon CPU, redesigned Adreno GPU, and Hexagon NPU.

Qualcomm says phones with both chips will come from leading global smartphone brands. That said, it remains to be seen whether the AI, gaming, and camera upgrades they promise will make any real difference for the average user.
item.description: Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme processor wants to run AI agents directly on your phone.

item.title: The Motorola Signature 27 is coming for Android's best flagships with some wild specs
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • The Motorola Signature 27 is powered by Qualcomm's new 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset.
  • Motorola's new ArcticMesh cooling system promises around 40% better thermal performance than the previous generation.
  • The quad-camera setup includes a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main camera and a massive 200MP periscope telephoto sensor.
  • Motorola hasn't announced pricing yet, but the Signature 27 is expected to launch in markets worldwide later this year.

Motorola has just revealed its first smartphone powered by the new Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, and it's called the Motorola Signature 27.

Motorola has been teasing the Signature 27 on social media for the past couple of days, and now we're finally learning more about the device. The Signature 27 is the company's top-tier flagship smartphone and the second generation in the lineup following last year's first Signature model.

Motorola says the Signature series is also adopting a new naming scheme, using the final two digits of the coming year for each new model.

Powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, Qualcomm's first 2nm chipset, Motorola says the Signature 27 will deliver flagship performance alongside powerful on-device AI, gaming, and camera capabilities. To keep all of that performance cool, Motorola is using a new ArcticMesh cooling system that combines diamond-infused thermal gel with a redesigned 3D vapor chamber.

Motorola says the new cooling system offers around a 40% improvement in thermal performance compared to the previous generation, particularly during sustained AI workloads, gaming, and video recording.

Speaking of cameras, one of the main highlights of the Signature 27 is the quad-camera setup on the back. It includes a 50MP Sony LYTIA 910 main sensor alongside a massive 200MP periscope telephoto camera.

There's also a new video enhancement engine that uses AI to create a real-time intelligence layer, automatically adjusting things like color tones by analyzing the scene before and during recording. Motorola has also integrated Qualcomm's image stabilization technology with 3.5-degree hardware OIS, which the company says should result in smoother and more stable video.

Audio is getting a major upgrade as well, with the Signature 27 becoming Motorola's first smartphone to feature Audio by B&O.

In terms of design, Motorola is sticking with premium materials and offering the Signature 27 in two distinct finishes. Pantone Cool Smoke features a woven texture designed to improve grip, while Pantone Capulet Green goes for a softer, more fashion-inspired finish.

Motorola hasn't announced the Signature 27's exact release date, availability, or pricing just yet. However, the company says the phone is expected to launch in markets worldwide later this year, so we should hear more about pricing and availability fairly soon.
item.description: Motorola isn't holding back with its latest flagship, and that 200MP telephoto camera has my attention.

item.title: Nothing expands Android 17 Open Beta to Phone 4a—full release is two months away
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Nothing announced that its OS 5.0 (Android 17) Open Beta is now welcoming the Phone 4a, 3a, and 3a Pro.
  • Users may find an update ~2.8GB, loaded with new features for the camera, the a new system typeface, widgets, customization, AI, and more.
  • The Phone 3 got into the Open Beta in August, and users with that phone should see a full release in mid-October.

Another new day means something to look forward to from Nothing OS. The company announced that it's now rolling out the Open Beta of OS 5 to more phones.

Over on X, Nothing announced that it's now accepting the Phone 4a, Phone 3a, and 3a Pro into the OS 5 Open Beta. Going by the company's timeline, these phones are right on schedule, as it listed a "Late September" timeframe for the Open Beta. What's more, testing should last for a little while. Nothing says these devices likely won't see a general release until early November.

The folks at Android Authority swiped the changelog for the Open Beta. That is, for the Phone 3a. It states the update is ~2.8GB on the Phone 3a, so the size should be similar on the other two devices. Much of the changelog mirrors what Nothing released for the Phone 3 back in August. The Android 17 test brings a dedicated Glyph app for the Glyph Interface. While the Quick Settings and home screen app management get refreshed, Nothing is introducing a new "three-color status bar indicator."

This indicator is for "scenes of sensitive access," location, AI processing, and more. Visual enhancements are rolling out across the board for Nothing's phones, as are updates to its camera. Users will find Filters and Tuning support for video, alongside Dual-View for recordings.

Some users on X have said they've had difficulties with the Open Beta. Basically, it's showing that there's nothing to download. It might be worth waiting a while before attempting as the beta comes online for more users.

Testing continues, but launch is near

There was hype around the Nothing OS 5.0 Open Beta for the Phone 3 back in August. This is the company's major Android 17 update, and there was a lot to go over. A new system typeface (Geist), refreshed system icons, better adaptive colors for your wallpapers, and more. Since the Phone 3 got its Open Beta last month, Nothing said users should expect its stable release in mid-October.

Most phones are getting that two-month testing period to iron out any bugs before it his everyone's device. In our hands-on, it was evident that Nothing was pushing ahead with a little more AI on Nothing OS 5.0. What's more, the company is doing so with privacy at the forefront.
item.description: If you're a Phone 4a user, Nothing OS 5.0 Open Beta is active now, and you can get going with all the latest Android 17 features.

item.title: Oh no, not again: it looks like Samsung delayed its One UI 9 global release
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Samsung has reportedly delayed the global release of its One UI 9 (Android 17) update for Galaxy users.
  • The company originally planned to release the update on September 21, but missed the date, and quietly changed its new plans twice.
  • Samsung went from a September 28 possibility to a general "September 2026" window, but time is running out.
  • One UI 9 has been in testing for five months, and users we're eagerly awaiting the release of the next major Android software/

Reactions have been in an uproar across social media and publications early today (Sept. 22). Samsung has reportedly delayed its major Android update, and we have a general timeline for when to expect it.

Reports have been fast and furious on social media; however, we're getting started with a post by SammyGuru. The post reminds us that Samsung originally announced One UI 9's arrival last week, on September 16. The Android 17 update was supposed to begin rolling out globally to more users on September 21 (yesterday), but that didn't happen.

This is where things get strange. Tarun Vats brought this up on X, too, stating that Samsung Thailand's blog changed the original September 21 date to September 28. However, early this morning, the company changed the date once again.

Now, September 28 is no longer present. Samsung has replaced this missed date with a general "September 2026" launch window. The blog reads, "In Thailand, the update will first be available on the Galaxy S26 series, Galaxy S25 series, and Galaxy Z7 series within September, with further updates to the Galaxy S23 FE later this year." It's hard to think one way or the other right now. Either Samsung is still sticking to this delayed September 28 date, or we're going to see it even later.

However, Samsung can't go too late into the month. September only has 30 days. So we'll either see the update on the 28th, 29th, or 30th. Either way, this development is extremely disappointing.

Surprise, surprise

To remind you, we've been dealing with five months of One UI 9 testing with Samsung. Testing for the Galaxy S26 series started for users in May. The company synced its beta across multiple regions, including Germany, India, Korea, Poland, the UK, and the U.S. The start was pretty light, offering users a glimpse into a few new features for the Contacts app and Samsung Notes.

Fast-forward to September, and we received the wondrous announcement of One UI 9's full release. Funnily enough, Samsung's U.S. newsroom post didn't mention a specific date for the global release. Makes one curious. Regardless, Samsung said it was pushing its update in South Korea on September 16. Global users were to follow, but it looks like we're all left waiting—again.

Android Central's Take

I've got nothing to say. That's not true. I have something to say, but I'd rather not. It's frustrating. That's also the sentiment I'm getting from users on social media, too. People are annoyed and tired and confused about the delay. If you remember Samsung's One UI 8.5 update, that was hounded by delay after delay. I can't imagine One UI 9 getting pushed back into October, but I guess I won't hold my breath about it, either.
item.description: This is getting tiring. Samsung reportedly changed its plans twice. One UI 9 has been delayed and now has a general "September 2026" launch timeframe.
item.author: nickodiaz@sbcglobal.net (Nickolas Diaz)

item.title: Who needs Prime Day? A bunch of Chromebook deals just dropped at Best Buy — check out my top picks
item.dc:content:
Fall sale season is swiftly approaching, but you apparently don't need to wait to score some exceptional Chromebook deals from Best Buy. For a limited time, the iconic retailer is slashing up to $250 off laptops from manufacturers like Lenovo, HP, ASUS, and Acer, making Amazon's upcoming Big Deal Days sale (October 6-7) feel a bit superfluous.

The devices on sale are no slouches, either. item.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: The choice will shock you
item.dc:content:
Apple
iPhone 18 Pro Max

The best for most people

While it's going to be a big adjustment for anyone who is used to Android, Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max is a tech powerhouse, packing in a bigger battery with faster charging than the Galaxy S26 Ultra, a faster processor, better cameras, and more features than ever. The biggest downside is that Apple loves to lock people into its ecosystem, so if you're still of the opinion that "choice is best" when it comes to your smartphones and accessories, Samsung is the better choice.

Pros

  • Faster processor
  • Faster charging
  • Larger battery
  • More eye-friendly displays
  • Main camera includes variable aperture

Cons

  • No stylus support
  • Telephoto camera isn't as capable
  • Heavy
  • eSIM-only in the U.S.
  • Apple ecosystem lock-in

Samsung
Galaxy S26 Ultra

The best for Samsung fans

If you're deeply entrenched in the Samsung ecosystem, upgrading to a Galaxy S26 Ultra is a pretty easy choice. While Samsung isn't exactly pushing the envelope for tech specs these days, it's still packing One UI, which includes more features than you'll know what to do with. It's an especially good flagship if you enjoy customizing your phone, as Samsung's Good Lock software is unbeatable for the job.

Pros

  • Privacy Display is an amazing achievement
  • S-Pen stylus included
  • Seven years of software updates
  • OS is more customizable
  • More features
  • Better camera zoom detail

Cons

  • Display has eye-comfort issues
  • Charges slower
  • Smaller battery
  • Worse ultrawide camera and portrait shots
  • S Pen design is poor and lacks Bluetooth

Choosing between the Galaxy S26 Ultra and iPhone 18 Pro Max? I'm about to make this decision much easier for you.

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra came out in March 2026, while Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max debuted in September. That six-month gap is enough to account for some major differences between these phones, but Samsung's lackadaisical attitude with its flagship phones in the past few years has finally caught up, and that means I'm about to do something I've never before done in my life: recommend an iPhone.

You might think I'm crazy for it, but Apple's latest flagship checks more boxes than Samsung's and, at the same price, it's hard to argue with the facts. Here's what you need to know.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Design, specs, and performance

Over the years, Samsung has opted for flatter and flatter designs. While the company thankfully got rid of the square corners on the Galaxy S Ultra series, Apple's curvier iPhone designs are far more comfortable to hold on a daily basis. But while those curves certainly feel better in the hand, the iPhone weighs a whopping 35g more and is nearly 1mm thicker than the Galaxy S26 Ultra.

Some of this has to do with the MagSafe magnets built into iPhones, but some of it is also because the iPhone has a 10% larger battery than the Galaxy S26 Ultra. And while 10% doesn't sound like a lot, real-world usage of both phones ends up showing a far greater difference in the end.

Category

Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max

Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

Display

6.9-inch Super Retina XDR OLED, 120Hz

6.9-inch QHD+ AMOLED, 120Hz

Processor

Apple A20

Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy

RAM

12GB

12GB / 16GB

Storage

256GB / 512GB / 1TB / 2TB

256GB / 512GB / 1TB

Rear Camera 1

48MP, variable f/1.5-4.0, OIS (wide)

200MP, f/1.4, OIS (wide)

Rear Camera 2

48 MP, f/2.2, OIS (ultrawide)

50MP, f/1.9 (ultrawide)

Rear Camera 3

N/A

10MP, f/2.4, 3x (telephoto)

Rear Camera 4

48MP, f/2.8, 4x (telephoto)

50MP, f/2.9, 5x (periscope telephoto)

Front Camera

18MP, multi-aspect ratio, f/1.9

12MP, f/2.2

Ingress Protection

IP68

IP68

Connectivity

5G (sub-6GHz, mmWave), Wi-Fi 7, UWB, Bluetooth 6.0, eSIM only (in U.S.)

5G (sub-6GHz, mmWave), Wi-Fi 7, UWB, Bluetooth 6.0

Battery

5,391mAh (physical SIM model), 5,567mAh (eSIM-only model)

5,000mAh

Charging

PD3.2 wired, 25W wireless Qi2

60W wired, 25W wireless

Dimensions

163.4 x 78 x 8.6mm

163.6 x 78.1 x 7.9mm

Weight

249g

214g

OS

iOS 27

One UI 8.5 w/ Android 16

Samsung's Galaxy S Ultra phones have had the same 5000mAh battery size for the last 5 years. Meanwhile, most Android phones have switched to higher-capacity silicon-carbon batteries that reduce physical size and weight. The Galaxy S26 Ultra at least improves charging speed compared to previous Samsung phones, but it's still slower than Apple's latest.

Plugging the iPhone 18 Pro Max in for 15 minutes gives it a 50% charge, while our tests have shown that the Galaxy S26 Ultra only hits 41% in the same time frame. That difference becomes wider when you consider that the iPhone's battery is larger, too.

Additionally, Apple's A20 chipset in the iPhone 18 Pro Max is at least 20% faster than the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 in the Galaxy S26 Ultra (and up to 40% faster in gaming). That, combined with Apple's new "next-generation" vapor chamber, gives games like Monster Hunter Outlanders special advanced graphics settings only available on iPhone.

Apple also sports a customizable side key and the camera button, while the Galaxy S26 Ultra offers a built-in stylus. Samsung has been placing less emphasis on the stylus lately, though, stripping it of its Bluetooth features and opting for a weird design that can only be docked one way.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Display and cameras

The Galaxy S26 Ultra's Privacy Display is a unique AMOLED display that allows the phone to dim specific portions of the screen so that they are not visible from an angle, keeping prying eyes from reading your messages or seeing your photos.

While this feature is incredibly cool and quite a bit of fun to show off to people, the screen quality has been degraded because of it. In my display review, I showed that the effective resolution, brightness, contrast, and the anti-reflective layer were worse than the Galaxy S25 Ultra, and some people even found that Privacy Display was uncomfortable to look at.

Neither phone is suitable for folks who are PWM-sensitive, but more people in the flicker-sensitive community have had luck using iPhones than Samsung phones. While both phones run at paltry 480HZ dimming rates, Apple does a better job of managing the intensity of the PWM cycle.

Samsung experimented with variable aperture cameras a few years ago on the Galaxy S9 series, but did not stick with the technology for very long. Now that Apple has adopted variable aperture, the iPhone 18 Pro Max's main camera promises to deliver crisper low-light photography and better bokeh than the Galaxy S26 Ultra's 200MP main camera.

Apple has also caught up to Samsung with several features, including an actual Pro camera mode. The iPhone 18 Pro Max's ultrawide camera and portrait modes are better than what Samsung offers, and the iPhone even lets you adjust the angle you took the photo after it was taken with its Spatial Reframing feature. Samsung's most unique camera feature is Horizon Lock, which is excellent if you take a lot of action videos.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Software and features

One of the most difficult reasons to choose the iPhone over the Galaxy S26 Ultra is the fact that Apple's iOS operating system is nowhere near as customizable or open as Android. Aside from general customization, Android phones like the Galaxy S26 Ultra support a wider variety of peripherals.

Apple mainly wants you to only buy its products, so many parts of the operating system are locked down, meaning third-party watches, smart glasses, etc. don't have the same level of access as Apple's own products. This is the reason I've chosen Android for the last 16 years, and the reason I will continue to stick with it.

There's also no denying that Samsung phones are substantially more feature-rich than any iPhone. There's a running joke every year that Apple announces features that Android users have had for 10 years, and that's really no different this year.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: Which should you buy?

If you're truly only the fence between these phones this year, it's pretty clear that Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max is the better option. With better performance, better battery life, faster charging, a better display, and tons of new features that finally caught up with Samsung, it's difficult not to recommend Apple's latest.

If I were picking from the huge selection of Android flagship phones, I'd definitely pick something other than a Galaxy S26 Ultra.

Apple
iPhone 18 Pro Max

The best iPhone around

Apple really knocked it out of the park with this release, upgrading lots of things we didn't expect. Bigger batteries, faster charging, better cameras, faster performance, and a comfortable design are just the start of a great experience.

Samsung
Galaxy S26 Ultra

A great choice for customization

Samsung's One UI is the most customizable smartphone OS available today, giving users the power to choose how their phone looks and operates. Pair it with Samsung's Good Lock software to unlock even more potential!
item.description: Choosing between the Galaxy S26 Ultra and iPhone 18 Pro Max? This year's winner is a total surprise.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Sutrich
item.dc:description: <p>Nick started with DOS and NES and uses those fond memories of floppy disks and cartridges to fuel his opinions on modern tech. Because of this, he covers both smartphones and VR technology, two avenues that split his passions right down the middle. From Nokia fan to Android fanatic, Nick has been writing about and reviewing smartphones since 2011. An avid gamer and equally well-versed tech head, Nick worked in the IT industry for 15 years, helping to further develop his technical knowledge, which has become particularly important in his fight with PWM sensitivity and deep dives into display technology. He's a huge fan of any phone that can fold in half and loves getting into the nitty-gritty with folding phone coverage for the site. He's also got over a decade of experience with VR gaming, having used the original Oculus DK1 and every major VR headset since then, passionately covering Android Central's Meta Quest content and smart glasses coverage with his weekly thVRsday column on Thursdays. Beyond that, you'll find Nick taking photos of anything and everything, from the beautiful mountains of his home to the chickens in his backyard, and using them to compare cameras to help you choose the best one.</p>
