item.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11: The best of iOS faces the best of Android
item.dc:content:
Apple
iPhone 18 Pro

The latest and greatest of iOS

The iPhone 18 Pro is the entry point into the iPhone 18 series and it brings loads of fantastic upgrades over its predecessor. The chipset is faster than ever before, the new variable-aperture cameras are a game changer, and the larger battery makes all-day battery life possible. Apple also added a ton of software features, though most of them have been on Android for years.

Pros

  • Improved processor
  • Battery and charging gains
  • Displays are more eye-friendly
  • Variable-aperture is a game changer
  • Apple promises five but usually delivers seven years of updates
  • Available in higher storage options

Cons

  • Telephoto camera isn't as capable
  • Heavy
  • U.S. version is eSIM-only
  • Apple ecosystem lock-in
  • $300 more than Pixel 11

Google
Pixel 11

Unadulterated Android

The Pixel 11 is one of the best base model Pixels in Google's flagship lineups. It doesn't have HiLight or UWB like the Pixel 11 Pro or Pro XL, but you still get an upgraded main sensor, a newer and faster Tensor G6 chipset, faster wireless charging, great social features, and useful AI tools and features like Magic Capture. It is also $300 cheaper than the iPhone 18 Pro, though it can't keep up with the iPhone's gaming performance or all-star variable-aperture camera setup.

Pros

  • Excellent new main camera
  • Useful AI features like Magic Capture
  • All-day battery-life
  • Faster 25W Qi2 charging
  • Great social features

Cons

  • Lacks UWB
  • U.S. version is eSIM-only
  • Runs hot when gaming
  • $100 price increase over Pixel 10
  • Only comes in up to 512GB

An Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11 comparison is like apples to oranges. Both devices run different operating systems and have very different ecosystems. Based on what you value in a smartphone, and how much money you've got to spare, which phone is better is subjective.

What makes this a difficult choice is that both phones came out a month apart, so they have the best of what Apple and Google have to offer, and both phones have different positive and negative attributes. Before making a suggestion, let me break down the cold hard facts and dive into the important aspects of what make each device good — or bad.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11: Design, specs, and performance

Looks-wise, both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pixel 11 haven't changed much over their last-gen counterparts beside getting a bit slimmer and lighter. Interestingly, between the two of them, they have a similar in-hand feel as both sport 6.3-inch AMOLED screens, weigh almost the same, and have very similar dimensions too. Neither display is good for PWM-sensitive folks, but iPhone tends to manage PWM cycles better.

The iPhone 18 Pro has a smaller battery than the Pixel 11, but phones deliver all-day battery life on average. The iPhone charges faster when plugged in, recharging 50% in just 15 minutes as opposed to the Pixel — 55% in 30 minutes. The Pixel also lacks UWB.

Category

Apple iPhone 18 Pro

Google Pixel 11

Display

6.3-inch Super Retina XDR OLED, 120Hz

6.3-inch Actua OLED, 120Hz

Processor

Apple A20

Google Tensor G6

RAM

12GB

12GB

256GB / 512GB

211 grams

197 grams

OS

iOS 27, 5-year update guarantee

Android 17, 7-year update guarantee

Both phones have 12GB RAM and start with 256GB storage as standard, but the Pixel 11 only comes in one other variant with 512GB. Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro goes all the way up to 2TB. Notably the iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 while the Pixel 11 starts at $899, setting them $300 apart.

Apple's A20 chipset is superior to Google's Tensor chipset in terms of raw performance and power, so the iPhone is better for processor-heavy gaming.

Google promises seven years of updates, while Apple guarantees five. In reality, Apple usually delivers seven years of software support, so they're evenly matched.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11: Cameras

The iPhone 18 Pro favors a strikingly different camera unit compared to the Pixel 11's camera bar, even though both have triple cameras. If you have trypophobia, the iPhone will probably trigger it.

The iPhone has superior camera hardware with higher resolution overall. Variable-aperture is the biggest upgrade on the iPhone 18 series, allowing users to have granular control over the aperture and depth of field. Low-light photography has also improved.

On the Android side of things, the Pixel 11 has a new main camera compared to the Pixel 10, but overall the camera hardware is largely unchanged. Pixels always take spectacular photos, as do iPhones, so this is a really tough battle.

Both devices have their own set of camera tools and features baked in. The iPhone 18 Pro finally has a proper Pro camera mode and features like Spatial Reframing. Google also has cool tricks up its sleeves with AI-based features like Magic Capture, the most attractive draw of the Pixel 11.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11: Software and features

This is the most polarizing part of the face off because iOS and Android are vastly different operating systems. Apple focuses on a more shut-off, locked in ecosystem that does not play nice with third-party peripherals, and that flows into the software, restricting customization.

Meanwhile, Android is a lot more open, and the Pixel UI is arguably one of the purest, most useful and fun versions of the Android experience. And, of course, Pixel users get access to a significantly more open and wider range of accessories.

At the end of the day, Apple might have introduced a ton of useful "new" features with the iPhone 18 Pro, but the truth is, most Android devices have had these features for years. The Pixel 11 is much more versatile and feature rich in terms of software.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11: Which should you buy?

Unless you're an absolute camera nut or gaming enthusiast, the Google Pixel 11 is clearly the better deal overall. You still get triple cameras, all-day battery, spectacular software, and seven years of OS and security upgrades, all for $300 cheaper than the iPhone 18 Pro.

Admittedly, the iPhone 18 Pro may beat the Pixel 11 at photography and videography, as well as heavy gaming, but this in no way means that the Pixel can't stand on its own. You can still game on it, though the phone might need a few breaks. Not to mention, the Pixel's cameras blow us away every time.

In the entry-level flagship segment, the Pixel 11 delivers better value overall.

Google
Pixel 11

The best of Google

Save yourself $300 and a lot more money you would've had to spend on "official" Apple accessories by getting the Pixel 11. It's a similar size, excels at photography, and lasts all day long. The camera might not be able to beat the iPhone 18 Pro, but it definitely is worth every penny and shines in its own right.

Apple
iPhone 18 Pro

The new entry-level iPhone

The iPhone 18 Pro brings major camera upgrades, several new software features, and a larger battery. It's a worthy successor to the iPhone 17 Pro, and better than the Pixel 11 in some aspects. Apple no longer makes a base model iPhone 18 though, so this comparison isn't entirely on even footing.
item.description: Wondering whether you should cash in to the Apple or the Google ecosystem? A good iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11 comparison will sort it out for you.

media:content.media:text: Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11
media:content.media:title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11

item.content:encoded:
Apple
iPhone 18 Pro

The latest and greatest of iOS

The iPhone 18 Pro is the entry point into the iPhone 18 series and it brings loads of fantastic upgrades over its predecessor. The chipset is faster than ever before, the new variable-aperture cameras are a game changer, and the larger battery makes all-day battery life possible. Apple also added a ton of software features, though most of them have been on Android for years.

Pros

  • Improved processor
  • Battery and charging gains
  • Displays are more eye-friendly
  • Variable-aperture is a game changer
  • Apple promises five but usually delivers seven years of updates
  • Available in higher storage options

Cons

  • Telephoto camera isn't as capable
  • Heavy
  • U.S. version is eSIM-only
  • Apple ecosystem lock-in
  • $300 more than Pixel 11

Google
Pixel 11

Unadulterated Android

The Pixel 11 is one of the best base model Pixels in Google's flagship lineups. It doesn't have HiLight or UWB like the Pixel 11 Pro or Pro XL, but you still get an upgraded main sensor, a newer and faster Tensor G6 chipset, faster wireless charging, great social features, and useful AI tools and features like Magic Capture. It is also $300 cheaper than the iPhone 18 Pro, though it can't keep up with the iPhone's gaming performance or all-star variable-aperture camera setup.

Pros

  • Excellent new main camera
  • Useful AI features like Magic Capture
  • All-day battery-life
  • Faster 25W Qi2 charging
  • Great social features

Cons

  • Lacks UWB
  • U.S. version is eSIM-only
  • Runs hot when gaming
  • $100 price increase over Pixel 10
  • Only comes in up to 512GB

What makes this a difficult choice is that both phones came out a month apart, so they have the best of what Apple and Google have to offer, and both phones have different positive and negative attributes. Before making a suggestion, let me break down the cold hard facts and dive into the important aspects of what make each device good — or bad.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11: Design, specs, and performance

Looks-wise, both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pixel 11 haven't changed much over their last-gen counterparts beside getting a bit slimmer and lighter. Interestingly, between the two of them, they have a similar in-hand feel as both sport 6.3-inch AMOLED screens, weigh almost the same, and have very similar dimensions too. Neither display is good for PWM-sensitive folks, but iPhone tends to manage PWM cycles better.

The iPhone 18 Pro has a smaller battery than the Pixel 11, but phones deliver all-day battery life on average. The iPhone charges faster when plugged in, recharging 50% in just 15 minutes as opposed to the Pixel — 55% in 30 minutes. The Pixel also lacks UWB.

item.title: T-Mobile and Verizon are both running excellent Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 deals — but which offer is best?
item.dc:content:
Samsung's foldable phones are more popular than ever before, and retailers all across the web are trying to capitalize on this success by dropping some pretty great Galaxy Z Fold 8 deals ahead of fall sale season.

The offers from Verizon and T-Mobile are particularly impressive this time around, but which Z Fold 8 deal is best? Well, as always with carrier deals, the answer isn't exactly straightforward. Let's break it down.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 256GB: $1,899.99 FREE with trade-in, new line at T-Mobile

Add a line with the Experience Beyond plan and trade in an old or broken phone and T-Mobile will give you up to $1,900 in trade-in credit over 36 months. That's enough to make the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 totally free! Both new and existing T-Mobile customers are eligible. View Deal

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 256GB: $1,899.99 From $59.98 per month (includes Simplicity Plan) at Verizon

Bundle your purchase of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 with a new line on Verizon's Simplicity plan and both the phone AND the wireless will only cost you $59.98 per month (after AutoPay and paperless billing discounts are applied). Only new customers are eligible, but no trade-in is required. View Deal

How do the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 deals compare?

T-Mobile:

For starters, it's important to note that, in the world of phone deals, nothing is ever truly free. Yes, play your cards right and T-Mobile won't charge you anything for the Galaxy Z Fold 8, but you'll still need to pay for the wireless. The Experience Beyond plan starts at $105 per month for a single line, although you can drop that price down considerably by adding multiple lines and using AutoPay.

It also helps that it's one of the best unlimited plans in the business, providing unlimited coverage and premium data with a mobile hotspot, free streaming subscriptions, and a ton of international benefits.

You'll also need to trade in an old or broken device to receive the full savings. At this time, Samsung phones dating back to the Galaxy S23 Plus will earn you the max credit, in addition to a number of devices from OEMs like Apple and Google. Check T-Mobile's product page for the full list of phones.

Verizon:

Verizon is actually keeping things pretty simple with its Galaxy Z Fold 8 deal. New customers who bundle the device with the carrier's Simplicity plan will only pay $59.98 per month for 48 months.

The plan in question gets you unlimited talk, text, and 5G Ultra Wideband data, plus you'll get 10GB of mobile hotspot data and coverage in Mexico and Canada. The benefits aren't as comprehensive as T-Mobile's Experience Beyond plan, but if you just want some straightforward wireless coverage, Verizon's Simplicity plan is a great deal.

No trade-in is required, although you'll need to be a new customer and use AutoPay to enjoy the full discount. Existing Verizon customers can enjoy the same deal, but the rate will increase to $85 per month.

So which Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 deal is best?

✅Choose T-Mobile's deal if: you have a device to trade-in; you're a heavy data user and you want to experience one of the best unlimited plans in wireless; you live in an area with good T-Mobile coverage.

✅Choose Verizon's deal if: you're looking to switch wireless carriers; you don't need all of the bells and whistles included in some unlimited plans; you live in an area with good Verizon coverage.

Samsung
Galaxy Z Fold 8

The future of foldables

The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is a sleek and lightweight foldable phone with a new passport-style design, outstanding performance from its Snapdragon chip, and a nearly-invisible center crease. Battery life has been improved as well, plus you'll get seven years of OS and security updates guaranteed.
item.description: There are a lot of Galaxy Z Fold 8 deals on the web right now, but these two are the most compelling yet.

item.dc:creator: Patrick Farmer
item.dc:description: <p>Patrick (he/him) is the eCommerce Editor of Android Central. After working in independent bookstores for the better part of a decade and using freelance writing as a side hustle, Patrick switched to writing full time in 2020. Patrick’s writing has appeared in the Chicago Tribune, The Hill, BestReviews, OddityMall, and many other publications across the web. He joined Android Central as the Deals and Commerce Writer in 2022 and now runs the site’s eCommerce efforts and coverage of major sale events. Although he’s written about everything from exercise equipment to turntables, Patrick’s work nowadays is primarily concerned with saving people money on tech. He’s particularly passionate about eliminating buyer’s remorse and taking subjects that can be confusing for shoppers — such as switching wireless carriers or buying a new smart TV — and breaking them down into simple, easy-to-understand terms. Whether you’re a veteran tech-head or a novice, Patrick offers honest, no-nonsense shopping advice with years of hands-on experience to back it up. When he isn’t hunting down the best discounts or digging through the fine print of a carrier deal, Patrick enjoys trekking around the Rocky Mountains, camping out at a brewery, or spending time with his beloved polydactyl cat. &nbsp;</p>

item.title: These new AI glasses have a brilliant privacy feature every pair needs to adopt ASAP
item.dc:content:
The AI glasses race is seriously heating up in fall 2026 with yet another new brand, but this one is doing something no one else has done so far. Vonder, a new company from the folks behind Viture and Oura, showed me its new line of intelligent eyewear that's coming to Best Buy shelves in just a few weeks, with preorders starting on September 28.

Vonder sets itself apart by ditching the camera, a piece that's become a privacy nightmare for some smart glasses, and instead uses a combination of bone conduction sensors, powerful speakers, and seriously intelligent AI to create a totally different experience.

Instead of capturing moments in photos or videos, Vonder Intelligent Eyewear captures all the thoughts you (and only you) have spoken out loud throughout the day and turns them into searchable, actionable information. It's a similar concept to MemoMind One, but with a far more private experience and more mature software, and they're going to be a huge hit if my time with them is any indication.

A chat with the founders

I spent just over two hours chatting with two of Vonder's three founders, Emily Wang and David Jiang, on a Monday afternoon in Palo Alto. The duo showed up with a briefcase full of Vonder glasses, showcasing a blend of every glasses style the company offers.

As they talked to me about their latest product, Emily, who co-founded Viture (some of the best smart glasses), pointed out that David was wearing the style I had just picked up, something I hadn't noticed at all because the glasses looked so normal. Even Ray-Ban Metas are a tad thicker than a normal pair of Ray-Bans, but these glasses had totally fooled me, and that's just the start of where Vonder got things right.

At just 30g, these glasses are by far the lightest smart glasses I've worn to date, making them the same weight as a normal prescription pair. It's the moment I've been waiting for, and I know a lot of other people have, as well.

But what good are smart glasses without a camera? Here's where the paradigm shift comes in. Instead of capturing moments in the form of photos and video, Vonder Intelligent Eyewear captures your thoughts as you speak them out loud via a clever bone conduction sensor located at the end of the temples, before the curved temple tips.

This ensures that other people around you aren't recorded without their consent. Consent is the biggest problem with smart glasses today, and Vonder's clever design goes a long way to solving it. You can even permanently delete all your data with one tap in the app if you want to.

The glasses have two switches onboard plus a tactile raised touchpad on the underside of the right temple. One switch is a power switch, while the other is a "meeting mode" switch. This second one switches the glasses' recording function from bone conduction to four microphones located on the temples: two forward and two downward.

This mode is intended to be used only for recording meeting notes or other conversations that are important and is paired with a tamper-proof bright blue LED on the side. Start recording, and it immediately illuminates. Flip the switch, and it turns off. Audio is deleted the moment it's transcribed.

Vonder's AI platform soaks in all the data and turns it into actionable items and summaries. Full conversations — whether they're just your thoughts or the entire meeting room's — are not available at any time. "Notes, not recordings," is one of Vonder's key tenets for ensuring privacy, and it seems to work impressively well in the two hours I spent talking to Emily and David.

The Vonder app and web platform store all these notes for future reference, allowing you to search your memories at any time. It's a full AI agent that's powered by every major AI platform to date, including ChatGPT, Gemini, you name it, so you know it works well.

The service sports a unique 3D knowledge cloud that links common topics you talk about. Everything is not only searchable when you need it, but also proactive. That means when you search using Vonder, it doesn't just come up with the same information that ChatGPT or Gemini would; it also adds your memories into the mix.

Vonder AI can even be connected to your Google account, letting it parse details from there. David showed me his AI-generated daily digest, which included a "know before you go" summary of my bio and articles I've published about Viture, all pulled from the calendar entry for u

It's the sort of personalized "superintelligence" that we've heard Google, Meta, and others talk about, and it's made possible by a pair of ordinary-looking glasses you'll want to wear all day.

Less looking down, more looking forward

As David Jiang was telling me this, he made it a point to highlight the brand's blend of fashion and tech roots. Emily Wang, who was also at the table, previously worked for The RealReal and NEIWAI. The company's other co-founder, Guillaume Hamon, comes from Rivian and Oura, while David himself hails from Google.

Vonder features European design, comes in six different styles, three different colors, two sizes for each style, and a boatload of different lens and color combinations for all of them. Unlike Meta's somewhat confusing product lineup, which features a mishmash of colors and style options unique to each line, everything Vonder makes is available in the style you want.

It's all part of making glasses you'll actually want to wear all day, including battery life that matches the part. Vonder glasses ship with a magnetic charging cable that lets them charge while being worn (unlike glasses that charge in a case), but you likely won't ever need to do this thanks to 16-hour long battery life. That's more than double Meta's best estimates.

And, of course, there's no denying the utility that comes with a wearable AI companion. Vonder is a 100% American company founded and based in San Francisco's Bay Area, another building block in ensuring you feel comfortable while wearing these glasses.

Plus, Vonder AI seems to actually be able to do "regular" tasks like play and control music and answer calls with your voice, something brands like Even Realities and MemoMind haven't been able to deliver on just yet. And if you'd prefer a pair of Vonder glasses with displays in the lenses, well, they've got that coming, too!

All of this adds up to the best pair of camera-free AI glasses I've used to date, and I can't wait to get a final retail pair on my head.
item.description: Vonder Intelligent Eyewear is redefining AI glasses by ditching the camera and doing something totally new.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Sutrich
item.dc:description: <p>Nick started with DOS and NES and uses those fond memories of floppy disks and cartridges to fuel his opinions on modern tech. Because of this, he covers both smartphones and VR technology, two avenues that split his passions right down the middle. From Nokia fan to Android fanatic, Nick has been writing about and reviewing smartphones since 2011. An avid gamer and equally well-versed tech head, Nick worked in the IT industry for 15 years, helping to further develop his technical knowledge, which has become particularly important in his fight with PWM sensitivity and deep dives into display technology. He's a huge fan of any phone that can fold in half and loves getting into the nitty-gritty with folding phone coverage for the site. He's also got over a decade of experience with VR gaming, having used the original Oculus DK1 and every major VR headset since then, passionately covering Android Central's Meta Quest content and smart glasses coverage with his weekly thVRsday column on Thursdays. Beyond that, you'll find Nick taking photos of anything and everything, from the beautiful mountains of his home to the chickens in his backyard, and using them to compare cameras to help you choose the best one.</p>

Start recording, and it immediately illuminates. Flip the switch, and it turns off. Audio is deleted the moment it's transcribed.

Vonder's AI platform soaks in all the data and turns it into actionable items and summaries. Full conversations — whether they're just your thoughts or the entire meeting room's — are not available at any time. "Notes, not recordings," is one of Vonder's key tenets for ensuring privacy, and it seems to work impressively well in the two hours I spent talking to Emily and David.

The Vonder app and web platform store all these notes for future reference, allowing you to search your memories at any time. It's a full AI agent that's powered by every major AI platform to date, including ChatGPT, Gemini, you name it, so you know it works well.

The service sports a unique 3D knowledge cloud that links common topics you talk about. Everything is not only searchable when you need it, but also proactive. That means when you search using Vonder, it doesn't just come up with the same information that ChatGPT or Gemini would; it also adds your memories into the mix.

Vonder AI can even be connected to your Google account, letting it parse details from there. David showed me his AI-generated daily digest, which included a "know before you go" summary of my bio and articles I've published about Viture, all pulled from the calendar entry for u

It's the sort of personalized "superintelligence" that we've heard Google, Meta, and others talk about, and it's made possible by a pair of ordinary-looking glasses you'll want to wear all day.

Less looking down, more looking forward

As David Jiang was telling me this, he made it a point to highlight the brand's blend of fashion and tech roots. Emily Wang, who was also at the table, previously worked for The RealReal and NEIWAI. The company's other co-founder, Guillaume Hamon, comes from Rivian and Oura, while David himself hails from Google.

Vonder features European design, comes in six different styles, three different colors, two sizes for each style, and a boatload of different lens and color combinations for all of them. Unlike Meta's somewhat confusing product lineup, which features a mishmash of colors and style options unique to each line, everything Vonder makes is available in the style you want.

It's all part of making glasses you'll actually want to wear all day, including battery life that matches the part. Vonder glasses ship with a magnetic charging cable that lets them charge while being worn (unlike glasses that charge in a case), but you likely won't ever need to do this thanks to 16-hour long battery life. That's more than double Meta's best estimates.

And, of course, there's no denying the utility that comes with a wearable AI companion. Vonder is a 100% American company founded and based in San Francisco's Bay Area, another building block in ensuring you feel comfortable while wearing these glasses.

Plus, Vonder AI seems to actually be able to do "regular" tasks like play and control music and answer calls with your voice, something brands like Even Realities and MemoMind haven't been able to deliver on just yet. And if you'd prefer a pair of Vonder glasses with displays in the lenses, well, they've got that coming, too!

All of this adds up to the best pair of camera-free AI glasses I've used to date, and I can't wait to get a final retail pair on my head.

item.title: Google's anti-motion sickness feature is finally rolling out to non-Pixel phones
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Google is expanding the motion-sickness feature to more Android phones through Google Play services.
  • You’ll need an Android 17 or newer device running Google Play services v26.37.
  • Motion Assist uses your phone’s motion sensors to move on-screen bubbles in sync with the vehicle.

Google is taking one of the more unusual features from its September Pixel Drop and bringing it to a much wider audience. Motion Assist, the company’s attempt to reduce motion sickness while you’re using your phone in a moving vehicle, is now rolling out through Google Play services.

The feature arrived on Pixel phones a few weeks ago, but the latest update to Google Play services v26.37 extends support beyond Google's hardware. You’ll need an Android 17 or later phone and the latest version of Google Play services.

For starters, Motion Assist places small visual bubbles around the edges of the display. Then, it uses the phone’s motion sensors to move those shapes in sync with the vehicle. This works pretty much like Apple’s own take on the feature, which has long been available on iOS devices.

The idea is to provide your eyes with a visual reference that correlates more closely with what your body is experiencing. This might lessen the mismatch that can cause motion sickness.

The appearance of the feature can also be customized, including the opacity, color and shape of the bubbles. Motion Assist can turn on when your phone detects that you are in a moving vehicle, or you can turn it on manually through Quick Settings.

The September 21 update is not solely about motion sickness. Google is also working on making it easier to transfer real-time health metrics from Wear OS watches to phones, making it easier to find Driving Do Not Disturb, and creating larger, more refined system emoji fonts.

Google Play Store v53.3 also includes a few extras such as local-currency purchases in Argentina, Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan and Ethiopia; changes to Wear search results; and the ability to add a pre-registered paid app or game to your wishlist after it launches.

You can find the full changelog on Google’s help page. Keep an eye out for the system update rolling out to your device over the coming days — your stomach will thank you on your next road trip.
item.description: Motion Assist just landed on more Android phones to end car sickness for good.

item.title: I thought phone-sized e-readers were a gimmick. The Boox Palma 2 Pro proved me wrong.
item.dc:content:
I have a never-ending pile of books to read, and I try to take at least an hour a day to read. That usually involves sitting on the couch with the Kobo Libra Colour, and while I enjoy using the 7-inch e-reader (a lot), it isn't what I'd call portable; I mostly use it while at home or on a flight.

This is the biggest advantage with the Boox Palma 2 Pro solves. As it has roughly the same dimensions as a phone, it is seamless to take anywhere, and I just throw it in my EDC bag. While I was initially hesitant to use the device because of the smaller size, I now see it as a huge advantage, and I ended up using the Palma 2 Pro much more than I imagined in the last six months. Starting at $399, it isn't an impulse purchase by any measure, and it costs more than most high-end e-readers; I like the DuRoBo Krono as well, and that retails for $279 as of writing.

That said, the unique size and feature-set of the Palma 2 Pro make it a great choice to use just about anywhere, and I'm outlining three areas where it's made a real difference.

The Palma 2 Pro allowed me to read everywhere

When I take out the Kobo, it is intentional. I plan my reading sessions and try to minimize distractions. That hasn't been easy in recent years because of a busy schedule and a toddler, and there are weeks where I don't get any reading done.

This isn't an issue with the Palma 2 Pro; I have it with me while going out, so if I'm just waiting around, I just use it instead of reaching for my phone. While I prefer reading in hour-long sessions, it's just easier to take out 10 minutes to read something interesting rather than get distracted by my phone, and the Palma 2 Pro made a big difference in that area.

The 6.13-inch E Ink Kaleido 3 panel is a delight to use, and it has the standard 300ppi pixel density with monochrome content. It has colors as well, and the 150ppi density is decent enough when reading comics on the go. What I like better is that it has adjustable light with warm tones, and it definitely comes in handy.

I didn't use my phone as much

I'd like to think I do a good job with phone usage. I have DND enabled throughout the day, and I try to be cognizant about how much I use my phone. That said, there have been enough times when I went down a Reddit rabbit hole and didn't realize hours had passed (r/watches is addictive).

This is where having a dedicated device like the Palma 2 Pro is so handy. The e-reader runs Android 15 out of the box and gives you full access to the Play Store, and it has a SIM slot that lets you use a data plan as well. But because it has an E Ink panel, you're limited in what you can do with the device. This is a good thing overall, and I found the size to be ideal to hold in-hand and read on the go.

I don't have to charge it daily

Look, I don't like charging devices daily; that's why I used the Find X9 Ultra as my daily driver, and why I'm liking the Pixel Watch 5. Thankfully, the Palma 2 Pro does a great job in this area, and the 3,950mAh battery easily lasts a week between charges.

This is a big part of what makes e-readers great in general. The battery on my Kobo Libra Colour lasts closer to two weeks before having to plug in it, and not having to worry about whether I've charged a device — particularly while on the go — is a big relief.

Honestly, I didn't think I'd use the Palma 2 Pro anywhere as much as I did when I got started with the e-reader. The smaller size is just so convenient, and while it doesn't have the same screen real estate as a 7-inch reader, the portability is unmatched. If you don't want to shell out quite as much cash, the Krono is a decent enough alternative, but you get a lot of additional software features with the Palma 2 Pro.

Onyx
Boox Palma 2 Pro

The Boox Palma 2 Pro is the ideal phone-sized e-reader to take just about anywhere you go.
item.description: Boox's phone-sized Palma 2 Pro reader has made reading much more accessible on the go, and this is one of my favorite devices of 2026.

item.dc:description: <p>Harish Jonnalagadda is Android Central's Senior Editor overseeing the mobile category. He started his tech journey at a very young age by tweaking Windows XP installations, and that hobby ignited an enthusiasm that led him into the world of PC modding. After picking up a Bachelor's degree in computer science, he decided to pursue his passion by covering PC hardware at VR-Zone, where he reviewed motherboards, video cards, and DRAM modules.</p><p><br>While he used iPhones initially, switching to the Nexus 4 served as the catalyst to explore Android's burgeoning ecosystem, and he pivoted to writing about mobile tech, joining Android Central's newsroom back in 2014. As a Senior Editor, he oversees the site's coverage of Chinese phone brands, enthusiast audio products, networking hardware, and storage servers, leveraging his engineering background and extensive experience testing mobile hardware to evaluate the latest phones and accessories.<br></p><p>In over a decade of covering Android, he has used pretty much every single major phone released globally, giving him an unrivaled view into Google's mobile platform. His specialty is Chinese brands; he's charted the growth of all the major Chinese manufacturers from their inception, and he uses that knowledge to share unique insights. When not testing the latest gadgets, he can be found reading sci-fi novels on his e-reader, and occasionally yelling at the TV in frustration as Arsenal squander yet another title run.</p>

item.title: Xiaomi 18 Pro's new privacy screen could beat Samsung at its own game
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Xiaomi has confirmed the Xiaomi 18 Pro will feature a hardware-based smart privacy display similar to Samsung's.
  • The screen will remain clearly visible from the front, while side brightness reportedly drops to around 1% beyond 60 degrees.
  • Privacy protection will also be able to work with specific lock screen notifications as well as floating windows.

Xiaomi has already confirmed that the Xiaomi 18 series is arriving very soon with a magical rear display. And now, the company has revealed another major feature coming to its new flagship smartphone lineup.

Similar to the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Xiaomi has confirmed that the Xiaomi 18 Pro will feature a new smart privacy display. For those who don't remember, Samsung introduced Privacy Display with the Galaxy S26 Ultra, which uses the display hardware itself to make it difficult for people looking from the sides to see what's on your screen. And now, Xiaomi is bringing similar technology to the Xiaomi 18 Pro.

In a teaser posted on Weibo, Xiaomi confirmed that the Xiaomi 18 Pro will ship with what it calls a smart privacy screen. Similar to Samsung's implementation, the privacy effect is built into the display itself rather than relying on software or a third-party privacy screen protector.

When the mode is active, the person directly in front of the phone will still be able to see the display properly, while someone looking from the side will instead see a much darker, nearly black screen.

But Xiaomi claims it's going one step further than Samsung here. One downside of Samsung's Privacy Display is that enabling the feature also makes the screen look slightly dimmer for the person directly using the phone. Xiaomi says its implementation won't compromise normal front-on viewing when the privacy feature is enabled.

Once you move beyond a 60-degree viewing angle, Xiaomi says the side brightness drops to roughly 1%, making the display appear almost completely black to anyone trying to look from the side.

Similar to Samsung, Xiaomi is also building software controls around when the privacy mode kicks in. For example, Xiaomi's implementation can automatically protect specific notifications on the lock screen, while the feature will also work with floating windows.

Thankfully, we won't have to wait much longer to see how well the technology actually works. The Xiaomi 18 series is set to launch in just a few days, so we should learn much more about the smart privacy display soon.
item.description: Xiaomi is stealing one of my favorite Galaxy S26 Ultra features — and making it better

item.title: Googlebook pre-orders begin: this is everything from Android sync to AI and price
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Googlebooks are finally here, and Google says pre-orders have begun as promised today (Sept. 21).
  • The Googlebooks feature touchscreens, haptic glass trackpads, backlit keyboards, and strong Android phone pairing.
  • The company says users can cast apps or stop and start projects from their Android phone on their Googlebook.
  • Googlebooks from ASUS, Dell, HP, and more start at $899; available at Best Buy, Google Store, and other retailers ahead of an October 4 market release.

In case you haven't checked your phone, it's September 21. Googlebook pre-orders officially begin today, and Google's full announcement is finally here.

Today (Sept. 21), Google announced that pre-orders for the first wave of Googlebooks have begun. The post states that Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo build this initial wave. Pre-orders are open, and laptops begin at $899. Each brand features distinct craftsmanship, ranging from custom keyboards to cinematic audio. Google states these laptops from these brands were crafted in "premium materials like aluminum, magnesium alloy, and carbon fiber, making them exceptionally light, sleek, and durable.."

These Googlebooks provide touchscreens with up to 2.8K OLED displays, haptic glass trackpads, and backlit keyboards. Powered by Qualcomm and Intel processors (depending on the brand), these laptops also offer up to 14 hours of battery life. It's also hard not to mention that the Glowbar is back.

Google says this illuminates on startup and offers information about your battery percentage, as well as fancy animations when talking to Gemini.

You also shouldn't miss out on what's powering the Googlebook: Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite. The first Googlebooks are being powered by this chip, delivering a 12-core Oryon CPU setup, clocking in at up to 4GHz.

Google is taking its Android software on the Googlebook seriously this time around. These laptops "bring the best of the web and the Play Store" to consumers, but everything you enjoy on your phone is right on your Googlebook.

The post states that when users sign in, everything moves with them. By "everything," Google means your "Android phone’s settings, saved passwords, Wi-Fi networks, and messages." Users can pick up where they left off with projects or booking tickets at a venue. App casting makes it easy to continue what you're doing on your phone, but on a bigger screen. Additionally, you can search your phone's files from your computer. The Googlebook's Files app lets users "view, search, and open files and photos" from their Android phone.

We briefly mentioned the Googlebook's support for the web and Play Store, but the company stresses this for the user experience. Major apps like Adobe Photoshop and Lightroom feel right at home on the Googlebook, alongside streaming services and games (since the Play Store is supported). What's more, users can launch AAA titles from popular gaming studios thanks to "a complimentary year of GeForce NOW included with every purchase."

Of course, Google wouldn't leave out its AI: Gemini. Googlebooks feature "Magic Pointer." If you remember its I/O 2026 reveal, you'll recognize this feature. Magic Pointer lets users bring Gemini directly to what they're looking at on their screen by wiggling their pointer. When it appears, you can give it a task to complete or ask for assistance. Among the major Pixel 11 features this year, there was Rambler.

This spruces up your text, cutting out any filler words you might've said while speaking. Elsewhere, consumers will find "Create My Widget" with AI, which will create a custom widget displaying information you want.

Meet the Googlebook

As previously stated, pre-orders are open today (Sept. 21) for the Googlebook. Users can pre-order a laptop from Best Buy and the Google Store, alongside other retailers. The Googlebook won't arrive on shelves until October 4 in the U.S. Consumers in Canada will see them on October 5 with the U.K., Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia. There are also several goodies you'll earn upon purchasing a Googlebook for Google AI Pro and YouTube Premium.
item.description: Googlebook pre-orders are open, and consumers are in for much-needed synchronization with Android for apps, projects, and more.

item.title: Google built the best $20 AI subscription for everyone, even iPhone users
item.dc:content:
One way Google entices you to buy its latest smartphones — including the Google Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold — is through its subscriptions. Like most tech companies, Google upsells you a subscription to keep you inside its ecosystem, but unlike most tech companies, Google reaches a large swathe of most people’s daily lives.

For years, Google subscriptions were fragmented and separate, and while they still are to a degree, this year has been transformative for those of us with multiple Google products. I personally had four different subscriptions to Google products on my personal account — Google One storage, YouTube Premium, Fitbit Premium, and Gemini Advanced — and in the case of the latter, it’s one that I often forgot to cancel the renewal on.

Now, Google has a new proposition: the Google AI Pro bundle. The $20 starting price tag will be familiar to anyone who uses ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude, or any other AI model. What will surprise you is how much value is packed into that $20 price tag. Even better? You can get up to six months free with one of the latest Google devices.

This is the best AI subscription for everyone, even iPhone users. Here’s why.

Google AI Pro bundle offers phenomenal value for money

Like any human being, I love a bargain, or at least the perception of one. The Google AI Pro bundle is the definition of an absolute bargain, especially if you use one or two of the services.

First, it replaces the previous Google One bundle. In fact, consider it the evolution of that, as it’s managed by the same Google One bundle subscription process; the subscriptions are now named AI XYZ. I used to pay $9.99/m for 2TB of storage and was very close to my storage limit, but now the new bundle includes 5 TB. This is shared across Google Drive, Photos, and Gmail, and it’s more than enough for 99% of users. The best part? You can also share this with up to 5 family members.

Retail price: $20/month

Then there’s the Gemini Pro access; this alone is worth the $20/month price tag. This gives you access to Gemini Thinking and Gemini Pro models, which are quite capable for most of your tasks. It also lets you build platforms in Google AI Studio with the same allowances, and it’s a great platform for average users to build tools and platforms, since integrations with other Google services streamline complex tasks like database management and file storage.

If you only need extra storage and a powerful AI model, the Google AI Pro bundle already offers the best value for money, but the three lifestyle perks included really tip the scales in Google’s favor.

Retail price: $20/month.

The three hidden gems inside the Google AI Pro bundle

Google’s integration into your daily life is second to none, and the Google AI Pro bundle proves it has finally cracked how to deliver value and inspire customer loyalty. The key is that each of these three was a standalone bundle that would arguably be worth paying for on its own, and at least two had already proven their market fit.

First, there’s everyone’s favorite service: YouTube. The Google AI Pro bundle includes YouTube Premium Lite, which is designed to make YouTube Premium accessible to more customers. If you want fewer ads, a more streamlined experience, and a few other perks but don’t need the full ad-free YouTube Premium experience, this is a great subscription… and now it’s included in this bundle. (Retail price: $9/month.)

Then there’s Google Health Premium, the real hidden gem in this bundle. Google Health Premium includes the innovative Gemini Health Coach and, crucially for Apple users, can integrate with and pull data from Apple Health. This means your Apple Watch data can mostly sync with Health Premium, and Google’s Gemini Health Coach can answer questions and help you understand your health. This is a diamond that’s only going to get better, and I love that it’s included here. (Retail price: $10/month.)

Finally, there’s Google Home Premium Standard, a service I don’t subscribe to — I’ve mostly given up on my smart home dreams because of Google’s general apathy toward it — but it could have value if you still have a Nest Cam. It’s mostly for those with compatible security cameras and doorbells, and it lets you access video history, receive smart notifications, and ask questions about it. (Retail price: $10/month.)

The best AI bundle for everyone, even iPhone users

If you subscribe to cloud storage or an AI provider, the Google AI Pro bundle is a no-brainer, as it objectively offers more value for a similar price. If you already subscribe to one or two of Google’s other services, or any other combination, it’s also a no-brainer: $70 worth of services for $20.

Here’s where things get really interesting, however: Google is working on Project Aura, which will be among the first Gemini-powered smart glasses. They’re launching before the end of the year, and Gemini allowances are presumably key to making the most of them. If you’re buying the new iPhone Duo, you're probably buying the new Apple Watch and may even consider Google’s glasses. All of these bundled integrations ultimately give you a wide swathe of products and services, many of which are best in class.

Personally, I mostly wear an Apple Watch, and while the Pixel Watch 5 and Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 both have excellent, unique features, the Apple Watch has saved my life, so it's hard to move away. Google Health Premium integrating with Apple Health, plus the included 5TB of storage, is enough for the Google AI Pro bundle to cement its place in my workflow, let alone the included YouTube Premium Lite and Gemini Advanced subscriptions.

The fact that it comes included with the Pixel 11 series, some of the best Android phones you can buy, the Pixel Watch 5, or the Fitbit Air is just an added bonus.

item.title: After a few quiet weeks, Verizon just brought back its best Google Pixel 11 deal — that's a FREE Pixel 11 Pro 256GB, no trade-in required
item.dc:content:
You probably wouldn't have noticed unless you're constantly searching for Samsung and Google Pixel phone deals like I am, but Verizon has had a noticeable shortage of offers over the past few weeks.

Fortunately, it looks like the lull has come to an end, as the Big Three carrier just launched a promotion that will give you a FREE Google Pixel 11 Pro when you add a line with the Unlimited Plus or Unlimited Ultimate plan.

Google Pixel 11 Pro 256GB: $1,099.99 FREE with new line on eligible unlimited plan at Verizon

The Google Pixel 11 Pro is a powerful Android phone with feature-rich software, versatile cameras, and seven years of guaranteed updates, and now you can get your own for FREE by simply adding a line with the Unlimited Plus or Unlimited Ultimate plans at Verizon. View Deal

Meet the Google Pixel 11 Pro

The Pixel 11 Pro wasn't a dramatic transformation for Google, but I'm certain it'll still end up on our list of the best Android phones of 2026. The compact flagship comes equipped with a vibrant 6.3-inch OLED 120Hz display and the new HiLight LED array for notifications, while under the hood you get a powerful Tensor G6 chipset with 12GB of RAM, some upgraded camera hardware, and the advanced Titan M3 security coprocessor.

As one would expect from Google, the Pixel 11 Pro also features the latest AI-boosted software features and seven years of OS and security upgrades, plus you get Qi2.2 charging support and a thinner and lighter form factor than ever before.

The problem is that this lighter build results in a smaller battery than last year's Pixel 10 Pro, and Google still wasn't able to escape the rampant price increases that have been plaguing the industry. Still, the Pro remains one of the best phones that Google has ever produced, the price hike just means that deals like this Verizon offer are more essential than ever before.

Why is this Verizon deal important?

This Verizon deal is notable for two reasons. First off, it doesn't require a trade-in, which is always a plus. Secondly, you don't have to sign up for the carrier's most expensive data plan to receive the full savings. Unlimited Plus is a nice mid-tier option that's perfect for folks who want the premium plan experience without paying the premium price.

It starts at $80 per month for a single line (using AutoPay and paperless billing), but you can drop that price down significantly by adding multiple lines at once. Unlimited Plus gets you unlimited talk, text, and 5G Ultra Wideband data on Verizon's vast network, 30GB of premium mobile hotspot, and the ability to mix and match additional perks every month for as little as $10 each.

You can also pay a bit more for Verizon's premium Unlimited Ultimate plan, which lands you all of the perks above in addition to 4K video streaming, international coverage, and more.

If you're already a Verizon customer or planning to switch, this deal presents an easy way to get one of the industry's best unlimited plans AND one of the best Android phones for as little hassle as possible. It won't be for everyone, but unless you plan to buy the phone unlocked, it's one of the simplest Pixel 11 deals around.
item.description: Verizon is running an offer that will land you a free Google Pixel 11 Pro when you add a line with an eligible unlimited plan.

item.dc:description: <p>Patrick (he/him) is the eCommerce Editor of Android Central. After working in independent bookstores for the better part of a decade and using freelance writing as a side hustle, Patrick switched to writing full time in 2020. Patrick’s writing has appeared in the Chicago Tribune, The Hill, BestReviews, OddityMall, and many other publications across the web. He joined Android Central as the Deals and Commerce Writer in 2022 and now runs the site’s eCommerce efforts and coverage of major sale events. Although he’s written about everything from exercise equipment to turntables, Patrick’s work nowadays is primarily concerned with saving people money on tech. He’s particularly passionate about eliminating buyer’s remorse and taking subjects that can be confusing for shoppers — such as switching wireless carriers or buying a new smart TV — and breaking them down into simple, easy-to-understand terms. Whether you’re a veteran tech-head or a novice, Patrick offers honest, no-nonsense shopping advice with years of hands-on experience to back it up. When he isn’t hunting down the best discounts or digging through the fine print of a carrier deal, Patrick enjoys trekking around the Rocky Mountains, camping out at a brewery, or spending time with his beloved polydactyl cat. &nbsp;</p>

item.title: This early October Prime Day deal knocks the Viture Pro 2 XR glasses back to their lowest price ever recorded — but how long will it last?
item.dc:content:
Deals on smart glasses can be hard to find, but Amazon attempting to change all of that with its latest offers. Weeks ahead of the Big Deal Days sale (sometimes known as October Prime Day), the retailer is offering the Viture Pro 2 XR smart glasses at a 21% discount, marking $81 off the normal purchase price and bringing them back to their lowest price ever recorded.

These are a good pick for anyone looking to use their AR glasses for gaming, watching movies and TV shows, traveling, or other AR-based activities. They also have the benefit of selling for far less than many other smart glasses options, making them a budget-friendly pick as well.

They also come with adjustable frames, three different nose pad sizes, and seven fit customization options overall. To be sure, these aren't the most powerful or versatile smart glasses ever built, but for most casual users consuming media or tackling simple work tasks, they're a great pick.

  • Prime Big Deal Days returns Oct 6-7: see the full list of deals

Viture Pro 2 XR/AR Glasses: $379.00 $298.99 for Amazon's early October Prime Day sale

Some of Amazon's October Prime Day deals are going live early, including a 21% discount on the Viture Pro 2 AR glasses. This is an affordable pair of AR/XR smart glasses that's well-suited for gaming, watching media, and hands-free activities while traveling.View Deal

✅Recommended if: you're looking for XR smart glasses that feature a user-friendly UI and a nice display without having to break the bank; you want a pair of glasses with a good portable case and easy stowability, as well as adjustable frames that make them extra comfortable; you want XR glasses that will work for Switch 2 gaming or other console gaming, and you have a budget of around $300.

❌Skip this deal if: you'd rather upgrade to a pair of smart glasses that are better suited for work tasks than for gaming or watching movies; you're looking for smart glasses with high-quality built-in speakers; you mostly want AR or XR smart glasses for reading and want something that will offer a good user experience when doing so.

The Viture Pro 2 glasses feature an expanded field of view from the previous generation, now offering 50 degrees and offering a less limited screen. Viture's glasses also boast some of the best XR smart glasses ecosystems in the game, offering a nice experience for users.

These boast a 1,600 nit brightness level, 1080p resolution, a 120Hz refresh rate, and they also feature filters for blue light, a more cinematic aesthetic, and a bright display.
item.description: Viture has become a leading manufacturer of versatile smart glasses, and now one of its most popular pairs is getting a hefty discount.

item.title: Vivo's X500 Pro Max just became the camera phone to beat
item.dc:content:
Vivo just unveiled the X500 Pro Max at an event in Shanghai, China, and there's a lot to like with the phone. The X500 Pro Max is the clear highlight, but there's also a standard X500, and the X500 Pro. With the Pro Max, Vivo is delivering a bigger phone with a huge 6.85-inch AMOLED panel, and an 8,000mAh battery — the largest on one of its devices yet.

It's the cameras that are the main highlight of these phones, so let's start with what the X500 Pro Max has to offer. It uses a 1/1.28-inch 50MP main camera that uses Sony's new Lytia 910 sensor, and it's joined by a 200MP telephoto lens with 3.5x optical zoom — the same as the X300 Ultra — and a 50MP wide-angle module.

Elsewhere, the X500 Pro Max is powered by MediaTek's latest 2nm Dimensity 9600 Pro platform, and it is a clear powerhouse. The switch to 2nm brings huge gains in efficiency, and with the phone having an 8,000mAh battery, it should easily last three days without any issues. There's also a bigger 6.85-inch AMOLED panel with higher resolution than last year (3168 x 1440), and the latest connectivity.

Just like the X300 Ultra earlier this year, the X500 Pro Max focuses on video, with Vivo bringing most of the features over to Pro models. Vivo says it has achieved vertical integration through what it calls the BlueImage Dynamic Imaging Technology Stack, with the brand working closely with Sony (who made the camera modules), MediaTek (to customize the Dimensity 9600 Pro), and ZEISS (to deliver gimbal-level stability).

The X500 Pro and Pro Max can shoot 4K240 cinematic video as well as 8K footage, and they use Vivo's custom V3 and VS1 imaging silicon to boost fidelity of images and videos. There's a lot to like on the software side as well, with the phones running OriginOS 7 based on Android 17 out of the box.

The X500 Pro is largely the same as the Pro Max, but it doesn't have the tele lens, and the standard X500 is based on the Dimensity 9600M, doesn't have cameras that are quite as good as the Pro models, but the 7,500mAh battery is great to see. The X500 Pro Max starts out at the equivalent of $1,045 (CNY 6,999), with the Pro at $970, and the standard X500 at $830. Obviously, they'll cost a lot more once they start selling outside China, and as of now, there's no telling when that will be — or what they'll eventually cost. That said, given just how good the X300 Pro was, I'm excited to take a look at the X500 Pro Max and see just how it differs.
item.description: Vivo just unveiled the X500 Pro Max in China, and the phone will make its way to global markets later in the year. With a bigger OLED panel, massive battery, and groundbreaking cameras, it's clear that the X500 Pro Max is a true powerhouse.
item.author: harish.jonnalagadda@futurenet.com (Harish Jonnalagadda)
item.dc:creator: Harish Jonnalagadda
item.dc:description: <p>Harish Jonnalagadda is Android Central's Senior Editor overseeing the mobile category. He started his tech journey at a very young age by tweaking Windows XP installations, and that hobby ignited an enthusiasm that led him into the world of PC modding. After picking up a Bachelor's degree in computer science, he decided to pursue his passion by covering PC hardware at VR-Zone, where he reviewed motherboards, video cards, and DRAM modules.</p><p><br>While he used iPhones initially, switching to the Nexus 4 served as the catalyst to explore Android's burgeoning ecosystem, and he pivoted to writing about mobile tech, joining Android Central's newsroom back in 2014. As a Senior Editor, he oversees the site's coverage of Chinese phone brands, enthusiast audio products, networking hardware, and storage servers, leveraging his engineering background and extensive experience testing mobile hardware to evaluate the latest phones and accessories.<br></p><p>In over a decade of covering Android, he has used pretty much every single major phone released globally, giving him an unrivaled view into Google's mobile platform. His specialty is Chinese brands; he's charted the growth of all the major Chinese manufacturers from their inception, and he uses that knowledge to share unique insights. When not testing the latest gadgets, he can be found reading sci-fi novels on his e-reader, and occasionally yelling at the TV in frustration as Arsenal squander yet another title run.</p>

item.title: The first Googlebooks are here, powered by Snapdragon X Elite
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite is powering Googlebook, a new laptop category built specifically for Gemini Intelligence.
  • Equipped with a 12-core Oryon CPU (up to 4GHz) and a Hexagon NPU pushing 45 TOPS, the platform is engineered to run complex generative and agentic AI directly on-device.
  • Preorders are open now for the first wave of hardware, including the HP Googlebook 14 and new models from Dell.

Qualcomm today announced it will bring its Snapdragon X Elite platform to the first Googlebook laptops, a collaboration with Google to power a new breed of computers built around Gemini Intelligence.

Dell and HP are the first manufacturers to release Googlebook devices, and both models are currently available for preorder.

The collaboration pairs Google’s Gemini-based software with the Snapdragon X Elite’s emphasis on performance, efficiency, and on-device AI. Qualcomm’s platform also features a 12-core Oryon CPU that can clock up to 4GHz and a Hexagon NPU that can deliver up to 45 TOPS, meaning Googlebook will have dedicated hardware for generative and agentic AI workloads.

Googlebook also aims to make Android devices feel more connected to the laptop. Qualcomm's press release mentioned features including Cast my Apps, Magic Pointer, and Rambler, which are designed to provide information from e-mail, calendars, and on-screen content. Native Android app and game support also broadens what users can run directly on the laptop.

The Snapdragon hardware also has plenty of connectivity and display support. It supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, LPDDR5x memory with up to 135GB/s bandwidth and up to three external 4K displays at 60Hz. The platform also supports 4K HDR capture and can decode 4K120 video.

Again, preorders are already open for the first wave of hardware, including the HP Googlebook 14 and new designs from Dell. HP’s Samuel Chang says the HP Googlebook 14 blends Snapdragon efficiency with Gemini smarts for productivity.

Should Qualcomm and Google fulfill their promises of smooth multi-device continuity and serious NPU efficiency, this shift could finally give Windows laptops and MacBooks a run for their money in everyday productivity.
item.description: Qualcomm's Snapdragon X Elite now powers the first Googlebook laptops, built around Gemini Intelligence.

item.title: MediaTek's new 3nm chip wants to power fanless, AI-first Googlebooks
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • MediaTek's Dimensity CX C10 Max is the company’s first chip for its new Compute Experiences family, targeting premium Googlebook devices.
  • The 3nm chip packs an all-big-core octa-core CPU, 11-core GPU, and eighth-generation NPU for demanding workloads.
  • The Imagiq 1090 ISP supports cameras up to 32MP, HDR video, smoother zoom, cinematic video, and continuous focus.

MediaTek is officially bringing its silicon chops to high-end laptops. The chipmaker has announced the Dimensity CX C10 Max, a new processor specifically designed for the upcoming new wave of AI-first Googlebook devices.

The chip is the first product in MediaTek’s new Dimensity Compute Experiences family and is expected to power an upcoming premium ultra-portable laptop.

The C10 Max is built using TSMC’s 3nm process and takes a very unusual approach to laptop performance, with an all-big-core octa-core CPU, paired with an 11-core GPU. MediaTek also brings its 8th-generation NPU that provides dedicated hardware for AI workloads to the platform, rather than just relying on the CPU or GPU.

According to the company's press release, the MediaTek NPU 890 can deliver up to 55 trillion operations per second (TOPS). MediaTek is promoting the NPU as the engine behind the Gemini Intelligence features for upcoming Googlebook hardware. The company says that keeping more AI processing on the device can also improve response times and provide additional privacy benefits.

The device has more capabilities beyond AI. The integrated ISP Imagiq 1090 is said to be capable of supporting up to 32MP cameras and introduces AI-assisted imaging features such as HDR video, smoother zoom, cinematic video, and continuous focus. That should translate to better video calls, livestreams, and other camera-heavy laptop tasks.

Connectivity gets a big boost as well. You get Wi-Fi 7 with speeds of up to 7.3Gbps, plus dual-engine Bluetooth 6.0 for wireless accessories and audio devices.

The larger promise is efficiency. MediaTek says the chip can help manufacturers build laptops that are thinner, lighter, and fan-less, while still aiming for all-day battery life. The first devices are coming, giving Googlebook makers another ARM-based option for bringing local AI to the heart of the laptop experience.

The announcement comes as Qualcomm unveils its Snapdragon X Elite chipset for the first wave of Googlebook hardware, including the HP Googlebook 14 and new models from Dell.
item.description: MediaTek's Dimensity CX C10 Max is the company's first high-end laptop chip, and it's headed for premium AI-first Googlebooks.

item.title: This tiny Gmail update makes dealing with verification codes much easier
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Gmail now shows a Copy Code button when an OTP or verification code arrives directly in your email inbox.
  • The shortcut can appear inside the email and directly in the main Gmail inbox alongside the message preview.
  • Google's new verification code shortcut is rolling out through the Gmail app on both Android and iOS.

Gmail now offers an easier way to copy verification codes directly from the app.

Android already makes it pretty easy to copy OTPs and verification codes when they arrive through the Messages app. But now, Google is bringing similar functionality to verification codes that land directly in your Gmail inbox.

The company is rolling out a new integration for the Gmail app on both Android and iOS that adds a small Copy Code shortcut whenever an OTP or verification code arrives.

Now, when an OTP lands in your inbox, Gmail shows a small card at the top of the email (below the subject line) containing the verification code alongside a Copy Code button. You can simply tap the button and paste the code wherever you need it, instead of manually typing it out or selecting and copying it from the email.

In addition to showing the shortcut inside the email, Gmail has also started displaying the Copy Code button directly in the main inbox alongside the email preview. That implementation doesn't seem to work every time just yet, but I've found the shortcut inside emails containing verification codes to appear much more consistently.

The feature has already started rolling out with the latest Gmail update on both Android and iOS. If you don't see it yet, it's worth updating the Gmail app to the latest available version.

Unlike the Messages app, though, Gmail's implementation doesn't directly integrate with Gboard for now, so you'll still need to open Gmail and manually copy the code. Nonetheless, it's a useful little upgrade that makes dealing with verification codes arriving through email much quicker.
item.description: Gmail just made copying verification codes so much easier.
item.author: sanujb6@gmail.com (Sanuj Bhatia)

item.title: The Nimble SHAREPOWER power bank splits a 10,000mAh battery in half so you can share it with others
item.dc:content:
Gadget Weekly

Join Namerah Saud Fatmi as she explores the cool, quirky, and sometimes downright odd world of smartphone accessories, gadgets, and other nerdy toys every week.

Forget sharing a KitKat bar or a pizza; Nimble lets us share power banks by splitting them in half. If you're having trouble digesting this bit of info, you're not alone. If I hadn't been using the Nimble SHARWPOWER 10,000mAh power bank myself for a few weeks, I wouldn't have believed it either. But it's a real product, and it's well executed.

It's a wild concept, and once you've let the idea sit with you for a while, you might ask why do that when a multi-port power bank can easily be shared with extra cables. But there are some occasions that call for such a shareable battery pack.

It's not cheap, but it's one in a million

At $79.95, the Nimble SHAREWPOWER 10,000mAh power bank isn't an affordable purchase. It supports 35W PD wired charging in total and comes in four colorways: black, pink, white, and blue. It's a very small power bank that can easily fit in the palm of your hand, even when whole.

When split in half in what is called Share Mode, both halves are 5,000mAh batteries, and each comes with a built-in USB-C cable. So while this might be a pretty expensive 10,000mAh power bank compared to virtually every other option, its splitting act sets it aside from the rest.

Magnetic pins keep the two 5,000mAh halves together, and when you separate them, you reveal a folded USB-C connector inside. This is attached to the half that has the display indicating the battery percentage.

The other half has a proper USB-C cable that's tucked inside like a lanyard when the two halves are stuck together, which is called Stack Mode.

Each half also has one extra USB-C port, so you can actually charge four devices altogether when the batteries are split. The two halves support 20W PD each in Share Mode.

A truly and properly shareable power bank

This is such a fun little power bank, and you can tell how much thought was poured into its design once you start using it. Imagine a day out with your friends, and you need to share a battery pack; the other person can just walk away instead of leaving their phone with you.

Whether it's friends or family on a longer vacation or a short getaway with you, there is always that one person who refuses to bring their own charger or power bank along and usurps your battery pack. The Nimble SHAREPOWER helps you preserve half for yourself in such scenarios.

Even if someone hijacks one half of the SHAREPOWER power bank for the entirety of the trip or excursion, you don't need to be side by side or in close proximity all the time. You can go to the bathroom without leaving your phone behind or waiting in separate lines, since this product doesn't require two people to stay anchored to one power bank.

This is easily the best part of the power bank.

A great power bank for group trips and holidays

The Nimble SHAREPOWER addresses the main issue with sharing a multi-port power bank with others: you both need to be attached to the power bank and therefore must be close to each other for a while.

This is obviously problematic sometimes, especially when on holiday with lots of other people. Someone might need to go to reception while the other individual heads to the restaurant. One person might decide to skip an activity and stay behind. I've faced this issue myself as I'm always the designated tech person on holidays, and there's always one friend or another borrowing my power bank.

There have been times when I needed to go to a separate location as my friend, and we were both low on phone battery, in an unknown city, with all but one 5,000mAh power bank to share. One of us had to leave our phone with the other person until it fully charged, then meet up at a designated location later. Obviously, this was quite a risky move, but luckily we had other friends to accompany the phone-less person.

This illustrates the usefulness of the Nimble SHAREPOWER's ability to split into two independent halves that function as two separate 5,000mAh power banks in Share Mode. You don't even have to worry about bringing extra cables along. So if you're going on a trip with lots of other people, I highly recommend investing in one or two of these power banks.

Nimble
SHAREPOWER 10,000mAh Power Bank

Share the love

Put an end to your forgetful friend or family member hogging your battery pack on holiday with this 10,000mAh power bank which is literally two 5,000mAh power banks glued together magnetically. Nimble even includes built-in USB-C connectors on both halves, despite the SHAREPOWER being incredibly compact.
item.description: Nimble is making sharing power banks easier than we ever imagined with the SHAREPOWER 10,000mAh battery that splits in half.
item.author: namerah.saud-fatmi@futurenet.com (Namerah Saud Fatmi)
item.dc:creator: Namerah Saud Fatmi
item.dc:description: <p>Namerah Saud Fatmi has been interested in technology ever since the days of the OG Razr Flip and back when the PlayStation Portable was the sickest console to have ever existed. Having fiddled with gadgets, PC parts, and techy tidbits since her early tweens, Namerah started sharing her expertise and opinions with the world in late 2018. Fast forward to today and she has grown into an even more curious — and seasoned — tech enthusiast with a penchant for experimenting with accessories, phones, and mobile devices. Her coverage as a Senior Editor at Android Central focuses on the world of mobile phone accessories, occasionally branching out into sects like gaming, software, hardware, and more. Before becoming a full-time writer for Android Central, Namerah was a freelance writer with bylines at other respectable publications such as XDA Developers, Neowin, and Good e-Reader. She also helps out Android Central's sister brands Windows Central and iMore on and off. Namerah is based out of Malaysia, where she lives with her four-legged life partner, a black cat named Bruce Wayne. Her hobbies include casual gaming, attempting to pet anything classified as an animal, chugging coffee, traveling profusely, and going on culinary adventures whenever possible.</p>
